title: Chart-engine spike & ADR (WebGL2 feasibility, Electron vs Tauri)
body:
## Context
CandleViewer commits to a **fully custom WebGL2 chart engine** (`ADR-0002`) rather than a charting chassis, because no surveyed library renders footprint text cells, a 200-depth DOM liquidity heatmap at 100 ms, or volume/delta profiles natively. That decision is the single largest schedule risk in the project (`docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` R2 render performance, R8 browser/GPU compat). It is paired with a second open decision: **Electron vs Tauri** for the desktop shell (`ADR-0011`, status *proposed*, decision deadline end of Sprint 03), whose only real discriminator is WebView2's behaviour under sustained 100 ms heatmap texture uploads.

This Epic is milestone **M0** of `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §15: a timeboxed, explicitly **throwaway** WebGL2 prototype plus a measurement campaign that retires both decisions with evidence before any order-flow feature depends on the engine. R0 exit criterion 4 in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.3 makes this binding: the prototype must demonstrate **>=60 fps p50 and >=55 fps p95** on the combined scene in Electron, or the Lightweight-Charts v5 fallback in ADR-0002 is formally adopted and R1 scope is re-cut before Sprint 05 planning.

No production feature ships from this Epic. Its deliverables are numbers, two decided ADRs, a committed (non-gating) benchmark harness, and follow-up tickets for whichever path wins.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Throwaway prototype in `packages/chart-engine/spike/` (branch `spike/e06-engine-m0`, never merged to `main` except the harness + report), covering three scenes:
  - **Scene A** — 100k-bar virtual model with visible-window draw and the LOD ladder of `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 (benchmarks **B1**, **B2**).
  - **Scene B** — footprint grid at realistic density: 2,500 visible cells x 2 numbers (~12,500 glyphs) via an SDF atlas (`§3.7`) with a Canvas-2D glyph-cache comparison arm (benchmark **B3**).
  - **Scene C** — 200-depth DOM liquidity heatmap, `texSubImage2D` ring streaming at 10 Hz over a 4 h trail (`§3.8`) plus a 30-minute soak (benchmarks **B4**, **B10**).
  - **Scene D** — the combined scene (A+B+C + 3 indicators + 50 order lines) that R0 exit criterion 4 is stated against (benchmark **B5**).
- Deterministic seeded fixture generator producing all synthetic data (bars, footprint cells, heatmap columns) so every run is reproducible run-to-run per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §7.1.
- Measurement matrix across **headless Chromium**, **Electron** and **Tauri v2 / WebView2** on the reference machine (`06-…` §3.1), reporting p50/p95/p99 frame time overall and per §4.3 stage, draw calls, uploaded bytes/s, GPU + process memory, and WebGL2 capability probe results.
- **ADR-0002** amended with the M0 verdict (custom engine confirmed, or fallback triggered); **ADR-0011** moved from *proposed* to *decided* against its five binding criteria.
- Benchmark harness committed to `packages/chart-engine/bench` and runnable in CI, recording numbers but **not gating** in R0 (per `30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 Perf row).
- Design: prototype-informed decisions on LOD text legibility thresholds, heatmap colour convention (green=bid / red=ask, configurable — owner decision #10), and the SCR-046 diagnostics overlay spec, all delivered design-ahead for E11.
- QA: benchmark methodology validation, reproducibility gate, GPU/browser compatibility exploratory charter.
- Security: STRIDE model of the engine + desktop-shell boundary; the shell-hardening checklist that ADR-0011 criterion 5 depends on.
- Closes open items **O1** (Electron vs Tauri), **O2** (SDF atlas size/glyph set, first measurement) and informs **O3** (coarse-ring resolution) from `26-chart-engine-design.md` §16.

## Estimate & budget reconciliation
The authoritative epic register (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3, row **E06**) budgets this Epic at **21 points** over the S01-S02 timebox. The child breakdown below sums to exactly **21**, inside the +/-15 % tolerance required by `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`. The earlier 42-point draft was a double-count of the roadmap budget and is corrected here by trimming scope, not by re-opening the register.

| Ticket | Pts | Ticket | Pts |
|---|---|---|---|
| E06-K01 harness + fixtures | 3 | E06-D01 LOD legibility research | 2 |
| E06-K02 scene A candles/LOD | 1 | E06-D02 SCR-046 + heatmap colour | 1 |
| E06-K03 scene B SDF text | 3 | E06-D03 a11y mirror cost review | 1 |
| E06-K04 scene C heatmap + soak | 3 | E06-Q01 methodology validation | 1 |
| E06-T01 runtime matrix | 1 | E06-Q02 GPU/browser sweep | 1 |
| E06-T02 report + CI harness | 1 | E06-X01 STRIDE model | 1 |
| E06-T03 ADR amendments | 1 | E06-X02 toolchain pinning | 1 |
| | | **Total** | **21** |

To hold the 21-point budget the following scope was deliberately trimmed (each trim is restated in the child ticket's *Out of scope* / *Scope trim* section):
- **Canvas-2D glyph-cache comparison arm (Scene B, E06-K03)** becomes a single spot-check configuration at B3 density rather than a second production-grade text renderer. It only has to answer "is SDF clearly better, clearly worse, or within noise".
- **Headless Chromium (E06-T01)** becomes a one-configuration baseline smoke arm, not a full matrix leg. The binding comparison is **Electron vs Tauri/WebView2**, because that is what ADR-0011 turns on and R0 exit criterion 4 is stated in Electron.
- **GPU/browser compatibility sweep (E06-Q02)** covers three GPU/driver classes (NVIDIA discrete, Intel Iris Xe integrated, one software/ANGLE fallback) instead of an open-ended device matrix; wider coverage is deferred to **E46 Performance hardening**.
- **Scene C (E06-K04)** is measured at the 4 h trail and 30-minute soak that B4/B10 require; longer trails, multi-symbol heatmaps and coarse-ring tuning (open item **O3**) are observations deferred to **E11 M4**.
- **No optimisation-iteration budget beyond the timebox**: if the bar is missed, the ADR-0002 fallback trigger fires rather than the spike being extended.
- **Design tickets D01-D03 are right-sized to decisions, not deliverables**: each produces one threshold/spec/number needed by an M0 scene, with the full design work landing in E05/E11.

## Out of scope
- Any production engine code — scene graph, plugin API, React bindings, stores, real WS decode. That is **E11 Chart engine core** (M1+), which this Epic unblocks.
- Real market data: the spike uses synthetic seeded fixtures only; no Bybit connectivity, no dependency on E08.
- Drawings, indicators, trading overlays, replay, profiles (M5-M8).
- Android / mobile (out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14) and any non-web client.
- Shipping an Electron or Tauri application: only measurement harness shells are built here; the real shell is **E10**.
- WebGPU backend (a contained future change behind `RenderBackend`).
- A full device/GPU compatibility matrix, long-trail heatmap scaling, and a fully productionised Canvas-2D text arm — all trimmed to hold the 21-point roadmap budget (see *Estimate & budget reconciliation*).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The combined scene clears the R0 exit bar in Electron
  Given the seeded combined fixture (100k bars + 2,500 footprint text cells + 200-depth heatmap at 100 ms + 3 indicators + 50 order lines)
  When the scripted pan/zoom/update sequence runs for 20 s in Electron on the reference machine
  Then p50 frame time is <= 16.6 ms and p95 frame time is <= 18.2 ms (>=60 fps p50, >=55 fps p95)
  And the per-stage attribution against docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3 is recorded for every stage

Scenario: The combined scene misses the bar
  Given the same run reports p95 frame time > 18.2 ms in Electron after the documented optimisation attempts inside the timebox
  Then ADR-0002's fallback trigger is declared, the Lightweight-Charts v5 chassis is formally adopted as an amendment signed by the Architect
  And R1 scope re-cut tickets are filed before Sprint 05 planning, with the M0 numbers linked as evidence

Scenario: The Electron vs Tauri decision is closed with evidence
  Given the measurement matrix has run all five ADR-0011 criteria in Electron and Tauri/WebView2
  When the decision deadline at the end of Sprint 03 arrives
  Then ADR-0011 status is "decided" with per-criterion pass/fail and measured numbers, not prose judgement
  And whichever shell is rejected is recorded as "rejected-with-evidence" rather than silently dropped

Scenario: Prototype code does not leak into production
  Given the spike branch contains throwaway prototype code
  When the Epic is closed
  Then only the benchmark harness, the fixture generator and the report are merged to main
  And the spike branch is archived unmerged with a note on the Epic, per docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md §5.2

Scenario: Follow-ups exist for the chosen path
  Given a verdict is recorded
  Then E11 (and E10 for GPU flags) carry follow-up tickets citing the M0 findings, so implementers do not re-derive them
```

## Technical notes / design
- Engine architecture under test is `26-chart-engine-design.md` §2: main thread owns input/a11y/DOM overlays; a render worker owns decode, model, cull, batch and GL against an `OffscreenCanvas`. The spike must exercise the worker path, because the `RunMode.inline` fallback has different throughput and would flatter the numbers.
- Precision model is non-negotiable even in the prototype: prices are integer ticks (`Int32`) relative to a per-symbol origin, times are `Float64` with a `viewportTimeOrigin` subtraction before reaching the shader (§3.3). A prototype that uses float dollars measures the wrong thing.
- All four scenes use instanced draws (one quad + per-instance attributes) as per §3.4; MSAA off, pixel-snapping in the shader.
- Instrumentation uses `Performance.mark()` / `measure()` at each §4.3 stage boundary, exported as structured spans (`06-…` §7.2).
- Reference hardware (`06-…` §3.1): 6c/12t x86_64, 32 GB RAM, NVMe, GTX 1650 / Iris Xe class GPU. Every reported number names the machine, GPU driver version, OS build and (for Tauri) the exact WebView2 runtime version, because WebView2 is OS-updated and results are only meaningful when versioned.
- Statistical method: >=3 repeated runs per configuration, compare medians of p95 (`06-…` §7.4 flake tolerance). Single samples are not admissible evidence for an ADR.

## Test plan
- Per-child test plans; at Epic level: the harness itself is verified to be deterministic (same seed -> same fixture bytes), the report's numbers are independently re-runnable by a second engineer on a second machine of the same class, and the delta between the two machines is recorded as the measurement noise band.
- No coverage gate applies to throwaway prototype code (stated explicitly per DoD §5.2); the merged harness + fixture generator do carry the package threshold (>=85% for engine packages).

## Security notes
- Threat surface is small but real: the prototype pulls graphics/bench dependencies (STRIDE **T**ampering / supply chain, `04-security-program.md` §5), and the Tauri arm introduces a Rust host and an OS-updated WebView (STRIDE **E**levation). Controlled by E06-X01/E06-X02.
- ADR-0011 criterion 5 requires a documented equivalent of every shell responsibility including the **OS-keychain bridge for the KEK** (`ADR-0009`); the security review defines what "documented, working equivalent" means so the criterion is falsifiable.
- Data classification: none — synthetic fixtures only, no keys, no PII, no exchange credentials. The prototype must not be pointed at live or demo Bybit.

## Accessibility notes
- The prototype is not a user-facing surface, but M0 must prove the a11y strategy is affordable: the DOM-mirror sync stage has a **<=1 ms** slice of the frame budget (`06-…` §4.3), and the accessible data cursor/live region design (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §6, `26-…` §12) must be measured, not assumed. Covered by E06-D03.
- Colour-independence is validated at prototype stage: delta gets colour + directional glyph, imbalance colour + outline, estimated data a hatch pattern — verified in E06-D01 so E11 does not inherit a colour-only encoding.

## Performance notes
- Budgets: B1 <= 12 ms, B2 <= 14 ms, B3 <= 16 ms (text batching <= 2.0 ms, <= 2 text draw calls), B4 <= 10 ms (upload <= 12 KB/s, texture memory <= 20 MB), B5 <= 16.7 ms (<= 40 draw calls), B10 peak <= 600 MB with no monotonic growth (`26-…` §13).
- R0 exit criterion 4 is stricter than B5 alone: it demands >=60 fps p50 **and** >=55 fps p95 on the combined scene in Electron.
- Degradation ladder under stress is defined in `06-…` §4.4 and is measured, not designed, in this Epic.

## Observability
- Harness emits structured JSON per run: `{scenario, runtime, gpu, driver, os, seed, p50, p95, p99, perStageMs{...}, drawCalls, uploadedBytesPerSec, textureMemMB, peakProcessMemMB}` committed as an artefact alongside the report.
- The SCR-046 diagnostics overlay spec (E06-D02) defines the in-app runtime counterpart of these same counters, so field diagnostics and CI benchmarks speak one vocabulary.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All child tickets Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] Actual effort recorded against the 21-point roadmap budget; any variance >15 % raised at Sprint Review with a register-correction proposal.
- [ ] M0 report published under `docs/plan/` and linked from ADR-0002 and ADR-0011.
- [ ] ADR-0002 amended with the verdict; ADR-0011 status `decided`.
- [ ] Benchmark harness + fixture generator merged and runnable in CI (recording, non-gating).
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed against E11 / E10 with findings linked.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated: R2 and R8 re-scored with evidence; R10 (key-person) mitigation noted.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review (Spikes present findings instead of a demo, per DoD §5.2).
- [ ] Security sign-off on the STRIDE model; QA sign-off on the methodology validation; design sign-off on D01-D03.
- [ ] Spike branch archived unmerged; no prototype code on `main`.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E02` — the monorepo scaffold must exist (`packages/chart-engine` workspace, tsup build, vitest, Playwright) before the prototype can live anywhere sane (`30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1: `E02 --> E06`).
- Unblocks **E11 Chart engine core** (`E06 --> E11`) and informs **E10 App shell** GPU flag tuning.
- No dependency on E08 (Bybit adapter) by design: synthetic fixtures only, so a feed slip cannot delay the decision.
- **No hard dependency on E05 (Design system v0).** E05 runs **S01-S04 design-led** (`30-release-roadmap.md` §5), so it cannot gate an S01-S02 spike without a same-sprint dependency race. E06-D01/E06-D02 therefore consume E05's **Sprint-01 outputs only** (candidate font + type ramp and the dark/high-contrast token drafts from `E05-D01` / `E05-D07`) as a **soft, non-blocking input with a documented contingency**: if the ramp, font or tokens change later, the cheap re-validation described in E06-D01 is re-run against **E11 M4**, never against the M0 timebox.

## Branch
`spike/e06-engine-m0` for the prototype (archived unmerged); `feat/chart-engine-bench-harness` for the merged harness + report. PR size guidance: harness PRs <= 400 LOC each; the report is a docs-only PR.

## Dependency graph (children)

## Risks

| R2 Render performance | The whole custom-engine plan collapses | This Epic exists to retire it inside 3 eng-weeks, with a costed fallback already written (ADR-0002) |

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: UX research: footprint LOD legibility thresholds and non-colour encodings
body:
## Context
The footprint LOD ladder in `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 degrades cell rendering as pixels-per-bar falls: **L0** cell + two numbers -> **L1** cell + one number (delta) -> **L2** coloured cell only -> **L3** hidden (candles only). The stated trigger is "cell text needs >= 11 px of height and enough width for the widest formatted number". That 11 px figure is currently an engineering guess, and the spike is about to hard-code it into benchmark **B3** (2,500 visible cells with text, `26-…` §13). The performance target therefore depends on an unvalidated legibility threshold: if 11 px is unreadable, B3 measures a scene no trader would use; if it is larger than needed, the engine is made to look slower than it is.

This is also the last cheap moment to settle **non-colour encodings**. `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §4 forbids colour-only signalling, and `26-…` §12 commits to delta = colour + directional glyph, imbalance = colour + outline, estimated data = hatch. Those glyphs cost atlas slots and a second fragment threshold, so they must be specified **before** E06-K03 generates the SDF atlas (§3.7, open item **O2**), not retrofitted during E11/M3.

Runs design-ahead of its consumers (E06-K03 this sprint; E11 M3 footprint work from Sprint 04), per the design-ahead rule in `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Moderated legibility study with the Owner plus 2 order-flow-literate participants, on static renders of **CMP-109 FootprintCell** and **CMP-184 FootprintSeries** (`docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` §7) at cell heights 8/9/10/11/12/14/16 px, in the dark theme and the high-contrast theme from E05, at devicePixelRatio 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0.
- **Output 1 — LOD threshold table**: binding minimum px height and width per level (L0/L1/L2/L3) plus the +/-15 % hysteresis dead band of §3.6; this is the density E06-K03 uses for B3.
- **Output 2 — non-colour encoding spec**: directional glyph set for delta, outline treatment for imbalance, hatch pattern for `inputSource === "orderEstimated"`, with the exact glyph list so the SDF glyph set can be frozen (open item **O2**).
- **Output 3 — number-format decision per level** (full vs compact `1.2K`), since §3.7 caches a per-cell glyph run and a format change invalidates that cache.
- Design-system contribution: glyph and hatch tokens added to the `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` vocabulary rather than living as engine one-offs.
- Catalogue corrections: **CMP-109**, **CMP-184**, and the **SCR-030** "low-GPU degraded" state copy ("Reduced detail: footprint text hidden below 6 px cells") — validate or correct that 6 px figure against the study.
- Stories informed: **US-CHART-001**, **US-CHART-003**, **US-CHART-008**.

## Out of scope
- Re-running the study against E05's *final* tokens/font — deferred to E11 M4 by design (see Dependencies), so that M0 is never gated on an S01-S04 epic.
- Hi-fi Figma screens for the footprint panel — that is E11/M3 design work; this produces thresholds and encodings, not a screen.
- Heatmap colour convention (green=bid / red=ask) — owned by **E06-D02**.
- Profile/TPO rendering, drawing tools, indicator styling.
- Implementing the LOD switch — prototype in E06-K03, production in E11.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Thresholds are derived from observation, not assertion
  Given the legibility study has run with 3 participants across 7 cell heights and 2 themes
  When results are tabulated
  Then each LOD level's minimum px height and width is stated with the observed read-accuracy that justifies it
  And any deviation from the provisional 11 px figure in 26-chart-engine-design.md §3.6 is filed as a correction to that document

Scenario: Every colour-coded signal has a redundant channel
  Given the encoding spec is reviewed against docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §4
  When delta, imbalance and estimated-data are each checked
  Then each has a documented non-colour channel (glyph, outline, hatch)
  And a greyscale proof render of a dense footprint bar is attached showing all three remain distinguishable

Scenario: The glyph set is frozen before the atlas is built
  Given E06-K03 needs a final glyph list to generate the SDF atlas
  When this ticket reaches Done
  Then the exact glyph set (digits, separators, unit suffixes, directional glyphs) is published and frozen for M0
  And any later addition is handled as a change request against open item O2, not a silent edit

Scenario: Contrast holds at the smallest legible size
  Given the chosen L0 cell height
  When cell text is measured against the most saturated cell background in both dark and high-contrast themes
  Then contrast is >= 4.5:1 per docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §5, or an outline treatment is specified that achieves it

Scenario: Hysteresis does not straddle the legibility cliff
  Given the +/-15 % dead band around the L0/L1 threshold
  When the lower edge of the band is rendered
  Then text at that edge is still readable, or the band is specified asymmetrically so it never drops below the readable size

Scenario: The design-system font or type ramp changes after Sprint 01
  Given the legibility thresholds were measured against E05's Sprint-01 candidate font and type ramp
  When E05 finalises a different font or ramp later in S02-S04
  Then a re-validation run using the same protocol is filed against E11 M4, not against the M0 timebox
  And the M0 report's threshold table is annotated with the font, ramp and theme actually used, so no downstream ticket inherits an unattributed number

Scenario: The E05 Sprint-01 candidate font is not available when this ticket starts
  Given E05-D01 has not yet published a candidate font or type ramp
  When this study begins
  Then it proceeds against the fallback font stack in docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md
  And the deviation and its risk to the threshold are recorded in the findings, rather than the ticket being blocked
```

## Technical notes / design
- Study renders are produced with Canvas 2D at the three target DPRs; no engine dependency, so this runs in parallel with E06-K01.
- Text on saturated cell backgrounds is expected to need the SDF outline pass (`alpha_outline` at a second threshold, §3.7). If the study confirms it, say so explicitly: it roughly doubles per-glyph fragment work and B3's 2.0 ms text-batching budget must absorb it.
- Define the widest possible formatted string per level; L0 width thresholds are a function of it.
- Deliver thresholds as a named constant set (e.g. `LOD_PROFILE_M0`) so a benchmark run records which threshold set produced its numbers.

## Test plan
- Not a code ticket. Validation is: (a) study protocol reviewed by the UX research lead before running; (b) results re-scored blind by a second reviewer on the same renders, agreement recorded; (c) greyscale proof checked by the accessibility specialist.
- Artefacts are consumed as inputs by E06-K03's B3 scene and by E06-Q01's methodology validation.

## Security notes
N/A — no code, no data, no credentials; synthetic values only in study renders.

## Accessibility notes

title: Design SCR-046 diagnostics overlay and heatmap colour/legend convention
body:
## Context
Two design artefacts must exist before the spike can report meaningful numbers or before E11 can build the engine's runtime surfaces.

First, **SCR-046 Chart engine diagnostics overlay** (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`): the `Ctrl+Shift+D` developer/owner overlay showing FPS, frame time p50/p95, draw calls, GPU memory, buffer uploads/s, WS message rate, dropped frames and a "copy diagnostics" button. It is the in-app counterpart of the benchmark harness's JSON report — the two must share one counter vocabulary, otherwise a field bug report and a CI benchmark describe the same problem in two incompatible languages. Its own budget is strict: **<= 0.5 ms per frame, sampled at 2 Hz, not per frame**.

Second, the **heatmap colour convention and legend**: owner decision #10 fixes green = bid, red = ask, configurable. `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.8 implements colour via a **256x1 LUT texture**, so a theme change is a one-texture update rather than a data re-upload — which means the palette must be expressible as a 256-entry ramp with a documented linear/log intensity mapping and an age-decay curve. **CMP-113 HeatmapLegend** (built from CMP-035 LegendItem) is the user-facing reading of that ramp.

Design-ahead: delivered in Sprint 01 for E06-K04 (Sprint 02) and for E11's M4 heatmap milestone, comfortably ahead of the >= 2-sprint rule.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-046** hi-fi spec in Figma: layout, counter list, threshold colouring paired with text (e.g. "below budget"), pinned/unpinned states, copy-diagnostics affordance, enable path from **SCR-118** renderer settings, hidden-by-default behaviour. Must satisfy the screen's existing design sign-off checklist verbatim.
- Counter vocabulary table shared with the harness: every counter name, unit, sampling rate and source, cross-referenced to the §4.3 stage names in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and to the harness JSON keys defined in E06-K01.
- **Heatmap LUT spec**: 256-entry ramp for the default (green=bid / red=ask) convention plus a colour-blind-safe alternative candidate (informing open item **O5**), the intensity mapping (linear and log variants) and the age-decay curve, delivered as data a shader can consume, not as a screenshot.
- **CMP-113 HeatmapLegend** spec: value ticks, unit labelling, side labelling, and the non-colour reading path (tooltip / cursor announcement carries intensity as text per `26-…` §12).
- Components touched: **CMP-024 Sparkline**, **CMP-036 KeyValueRow**, **CMP-069 InfoPanel**, **CMP-178 SystemHealthTile** (SCR-046) and **CMP-035 LegendItem**, **CMP-113 HeatmapLegend** (heatmap).
- Stories informed: **US-SET-008**, **US-OBS-002** (diagnostics overlay); **US-CHART-001**, **US-CHART-006** (engine surfaces).

## Out of scope
- Implementing SCR-046 against the built E05 component library (that is E11); this ticket ships a token-referential spec only.
- The DOM ladder and heatmap *panel* design (SCR-050 and the DOM domain) — this ticket covers only the colour ramp and legend that the engine renders.
- Implementing the overlay — E11 builds it; the spike only uses the counter vocabulary.
- Backend observability dashboards (E04) — SCR-046 is client-side engine telemetry only.
- Final colour-blind-safe palette selection, which `26-…` §16 assigns to the M8 a11y pass (open item **O5**); this ticket only supplies a candidate.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Overlay and harness speak one vocabulary
  Given the SCR-046 counter list and the E06-K01 harness JSON schema
  When the two are diffed
  Then every overlay counter maps to exactly one harness key with the same name, unit and definition
  And any counter present in only one of them is either added to both or explicitly justified in the spec

Scenario: Thresholds are never colour-only
  Given a counter exceeds its budget from docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3
  When the overlay renders that counter
  Then the breach is shown with text ("above budget") as well as colour
  And the overlay remains readable in the high-contrast theme

Scenario: The LUT is machine-consumable
  Given the heatmap colour spec
  When an engineer implements the 256x1 LUT texture
  Then they can generate it directly from the delivered ramp definition without sampling a picture
  And switching the bid/ask convention is expressed as swapping ramp halves, matching the one-texture-update design in 26-chart-engine-design.md §3.8

Scenario: The overlay cannot flood a screen reader
  Given the overlay is pinned open and values update at 2 Hz
  When a screen reader is active
  Then values are exposed as a static readable table with polite (not assertive) updates, per the SCR-046 a11y note
```

## Technical notes / design
- SCR-046 sampling is 2 Hz and the whole overlay costs <= 0.5 ms/frame; the design must therefore avoid per-frame sparkline redraws — CMP-024 Sparkline updates on the 2 Hz tick with a fixed-length ring of samples.
- Counter definitions must be unambiguous: "frame time" is the worker's render-loop wall time including GL submission, not rAF-to-rAF delta; "draw calls" counts `drawArraysInstanced`/`drawElementsInstanced` invocations per frame; "GPU memory" is an estimate derived from tracked buffer/texture allocations, labelled as an estimate in the UI.
- "Copy diagnostics" must produce the same JSON shape the harness writes, so a user-submitted bug report can be diffed against a CI baseline.
- LUT: the ramp is defined in a perceptually uniform space and converted to sRGB at generation time; log intensity mapping is `t = log1p(v * k) / log1p(k)` with `k` a documented constant so shader and legend agree exactly.

## Test plan
- Design QA against the SCR-046 sign-off checklist in `14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- The LUT ramp is validated by generating the 256x1 PNG from the spec and confirming a round-trip: legend tick values map to the same colours the shader produces for those intensities.
- Contrast checks on overlay text in dark and high-contrast themes.
- Feeds E06-K04 (heatmap scene) and E06-Q01 (methodology validation).

## Security notes
"Copy diagnostics" is the one real threat surface: the payload must contain **no** symbol-identifying account context, no user identifiers, no correlation IDs tied to orders — it is engine telemetry only (STRIDE **I**nformation disclosure, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5). The spec must state the exact allowed field list; E06-X01's threat model reviews it.

## Accessibility notes
- Overlay is a text panel, not a canvas; updates polite, never assertive; pinnable and readable as a static table (SCR-046 a11y note).
- All threshold states carry text in addition to colour (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §4).
- Heatmap intensity must be available as text via tooltip and the cursor announcement (`26-…` §12), so the legend is not the only path to the value.

## Performance notes
- Overlay budget: <= 0.5 ms/frame, 2 Hz sampling (SCR-046).
- Heatmap targets the ticket informs: **B4** p95 <= 10 ms, upload <= 12 KB/s, texture memory <= 20 MB.

## Observability
Defines the client-side counter vocabulary used by both SCR-046 and the harness report, and the `diagnostics.overlay_toggled` / `diagnostics.snapshot_copied` analytics events already declared on SCR-046.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Figma hi-fi for SCR-046 published; every box on the screen's design sign-off checklist ticked.
- [ ] Counter vocabulary table merged and referenced from both the harness (E06-K01) and `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-046.

- [ ] Colour-blind-safe candidate recorded against open item **O5**.
- [ ] Design sign-off (CDO or delegate) and accessibility review comment recorded.

This ticket specs SCR-046 and the heatmap LUT **against E05's Sprint-01 token drafts** (`E05-D01` colour/spacing/type variables) and references CMP-024/036/069/178 by ID and state rather than by implemented code. The spec is written **token-referential** (`--cv-*` variable names, never literal hex), so a later token change re-themes it for free; only the contrast checks need re-running, and that re-check rides along with `E05-D04` instead of blocking M0.
- `blocked_by: E06-K01` — the harness JSON schema is one half of the shared counter vocabulary; specifying the overlay before it exists would guarantee a mismatch.

title: A11y design review: cost and shape of the engine DOM-mirror layer
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3 allocates the **DOM-mirror (a11y layer) sync** exactly **1 ms** of the 16.6 ms frame budget, and adds a hard rule in §4.4: desyncing the DOM-mirror from what is visually rendered is *never acceptable*. `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §12 specifies what that mirror is — a visually hidden `<table>` exposing the visible window capped at 200 rows, a keyboard data cursor with `aria-live="polite"` announcements throttled to 1 per 250 ms, and a `role="application"` wrapper. `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §6 is the governing canvas/WebGL strategy.

Every other epic treats this as settled. It is not: nobody has measured what mirroring 200 rows of a live-updating window costs on the main thread while the worker is rendering at 60 fps, nor whether 250 ms throttling is usable when a trader is arrowing across bars quickly, nor what happens to the mirror during the LOD degradation ladder (if footprint text is hidden at L2, does the mirror still expose per-cell values, and if so is the mirror now *more* informative than the canvas?).

M0 is the only point where this can be measured cheaply, before E11 builds the production layer and before **US-CHART-014** (Accessible chart data alternative, Must) and **SCR-045** (Chart data-table alternative) are designed in detail. This ticket rides the prototype to get real numbers and settle the shape.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Instrumented DOM-mirror stub added to the E06-K04 prototype scene: 200-row hidden table bound to the visible window, updated per frame, with `Performance.measure` spans so its cost lands in the §4.3 stage attribution alongside the render stages.
- Measurement: main-thread cost of mirror sync at 60 fps, for a static view, a continuous pan, and a live-update storm (20 data messages/s), in all three runtimes.
- Design decision record on **announcement throttling**: validate or revise the 250 ms / 1-per-250 ms figure (`26-…` §12) and the "<= 2 announcements per second" NFR on **US-CHART-008**, using a screen-reader walkthrough with NVDA and VoiceOver against the prototype.
- Design decision record on **mirror behaviour under LOD degradation**: what the mirror exposes at L0/L1/L2/L3, and whether parity with the canvas or informational superiority is the rule (this is a product decision with an a11y consequence, so it needs a written answer, not an implementation accident).
- Early shape for **SCR-045** (Chart data-table alternative) and **CMP-180 ChartRoot**'s focus contract: `role="application"` wrapper, `aria-label` composition, tab-entry behaviour, and the relationship between crosshair position and the table's focused row (US-CHART-014 requires bidirectional sync).
- Stories informed: **US-CHART-008**, **US-CHART-014**; screens **SCR-030**, **SCR-045**; components **CMP-180**, **CMP-225**, **CMP-227**, **CMP-032 VisuallyHidden-class utility** and the focus-ring utility used by canvas surrogates.

## Out of scope
- Building the production accessibility layer — that is E11's M8 milestone.
- Full hi-fi design of SCR-045 — only its structural shape and sync contract are settled here.
- Footprint per-cell surrogate nodes (CMP-109's cell-level `aria-label` behaviour) beyond measuring whether per-cell mirroring is affordable at all.
- Screen-reader support matrix decisions beyond NVDA + VoiceOver (the protocol in `05-accessibility-standard.md` §8 governs the full matrix later).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The 1 ms budget is validated with numbers
  Given the instrumented DOM-mirror stub running against the combined prototype scene
  When a 20 s continuous-pan run is measured in Electron on the reference machine
  Then the mirror-sync stage's p95 cost is reported and compared to the 1 ms allocation in docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3
  And if it exceeds 1 ms, a concrete mitigation (windowing depth, update coalescing, or a lower mirror cadence) is specified with its own measured cost

Scenario: Announcement cadence is usable, not just compliant
  Given a screen-reader user arrows across bars at a realistic speed
  When announcements are throttled at the candidate interval
  Then the final state is always announced (no lost last update) per 26-chart-engine-design.md §12
  And the reviewer confirms the cadence is neither flooding nor lagging, with the chosen interval recorded

Scenario: Mirror behaviour under LOD is defined, not emergent
  Given the engine has degraded footprint rendering to L2 (coloured cells, no text)
  When the mirror is inspected
  Then the specification states exactly what the mirror exposes at that level and why
  And the rule is consistent with docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.4 (the mirror never desyncs from what is rendered)

Scenario: The mirror survives the degraded-2d profile
  Given the capability probe selects the degraded-2d render profile
  When the chart renders
  Then the accessible layer is unchanged in content and behaviour, confirming a11y is not coupled to the GL path
```

## Technical notes / design
- The mirror is main-thread work by construction (the worker has no DOM), so its cost competes with React, not with GL. Measure it on the main thread's timeline, not the worker's, and report both so the combined picture is honest.
- Windowing: cap at 200 rows (`26-…` §12). Test whether a smaller window (e.g. 60 rows centred on the cursor) is materially cheaper — if it is, that is the mitigation lever.
- Update coalescing: the mirror does not need per-frame fidelity for rows the user is not on; a candidate design is "cursor row updated at interaction cadence, remaining rows at 4 Hz", which must be checked against the never-desync rule.
- Announcements: use one `aria-live="polite"` region with last-write-wins semantics, so throttling can never drop the final state.
- `role="application"` on the wrapper is deliberate (it hands keystrokes to the app rather than the screen reader's browse mode) and must be paired with a documented, discoverable escape path; verify this in the walkthrough.

## Test plan
- Measurement runs: static / pan / update-storm x 3 runtimes, >= 3 repetitions, medians of p95 reported (`06-…` §7.4).
- Manual screen-reader walkthrough per the protocol in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §8, with NVDA (Windows) and VoiceOver (macOS), findings logged per scenario.
- axe-core run against the prototype page to confirm the hidden table and live region produce no violations (this is a prototype, so the bar is "no violations attributable to the mirror design", not full page conformance).
- Results feed E06-T02's report as a dedicated section.

## Security notes
N/A for data — synthetic fixtures only. One note: the hidden mirror table reproduces on-screen values into the DOM, so in the production engine it inherits whatever data classification the chart itself carries; recorded here so E11 does not treat the mirror as an invisible, unclassified surface.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is the a11y review for the Epic. It closes: keyboard reachability of the canvas, the data-cursor announcement contract, the DOM-mirror windowing rule, focus-visible treatment for canvas surrogates, and the behaviour of all of the above under `prefers-reduced-motion` (momentum disabled, instant snapping — `26-…` §12), ensuring E11 inherits measured decisions rather than aspirations.

## Performance notes
Budget under test: **<= 1 ms/frame** DOM-mirror sync (`06-…` §4.3). Secondary: announcements <= 2/s (US-CHART-008 NFR), table virtualisation must keep the view >= 55 fps (US-CHART-014 NFR).

## Observability
Mirror-sync duration is added as a named stage in the harness JSON and in the SCR-046 counter vocabulary (E06-D02), so a11y cost is visible in every future benchmark rather than being invisible overhead.

title: Build M0 benchmark harness and deterministic seeded fixture generator
body:
## Context
Every number this Epic produces, and therefore both ADR decisions, rests on the harness built here. `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §7.1 is explicit that ad hoc DevTools profiling is not acceptable: the benchmark must be a mode built into the chart-engine package, driving a scripted sequence over a **version-controlled, deterministically seeded** synthetic dataset, reporting p50/p95/p99 overall and per §4.3 stage. §7.4 adds the statistical rules (>= 3 repeated runs, compare medians of p95) that keep CI-runner noise from producing false verdicts.

The fixture generator matters as much as the harness. If the synthetic data is not reproducible byte-for-byte from a seed, two engineers measuring on two machines are not measuring the same thing, and the M0 report is unfalsifiable — which is exactly what an ADR must not be.

This is the first child of E06 to start and it gates the three scene spikes (K02/K03/K04), the QA methodology validation (Q01) and the diagnostics counter vocabulary (D02).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/chart-engine/bench/` — harness runnable headless via Playwright + Chromium with a fixed GPU flag set (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §13), and as an Electron and a Tauri target for E06-T01.
- **Fixture generator** in `packages/fixtures` (or `packages/chart-engine/bench/fixtures` if the shared package does not yet exist in E02's scaffold — state which in the PR):
  - 100k synthetic OHLCV bars with realistic volatility clustering and gaps, prices emitted as **integer ticks** with a per-symbol origin (never float dollars — `26-…` §3.3 precision rule).
  - Footprint cell stream at realistic density: enough cells that 2,500 are visible at the L0 threshold set by **E06-D01**, with bid/ask/trade-count per cell.
  - 200-depth heatmap column stream at 100 ms cadence covering a 4 h trail, plus a 30-minute continuation for the B10 soak.
  - Deterministic: same seed -> byte-identical output, asserted by a hash test.
- **Scripted driver sequences** (one per benchmark): continuous pan at 1000 px/s (B1), wheel zoom sweep 0.1 -> 50 px/bar (B2), static footprint hold with periodic updates (B3), heatmap streaming with panning (B4), combined scene (B5), live update storm 20 msg/s x 6 stores (B7), cold init to first frame (B9), 30-minute soak (B10).
- **Instrumentation**: `Performance.mark()`/`measure()` at every §4.3 stage boundary — input handling, data-window recompute, candle geometry, footprint text/geometry, heatmap upload, pane redraw, overlay redraw, DOM-mirror sync, composite+present — exported as structured spans (`06-…` §7.2).
- **Report writer**: one JSON per run — `{scenario, runtime, runtimeVersion, gpu, driver, os, seed, lodProfile, repetitions, p50, p95, p99, perStageMs{}, drawCalls, uploadedBytesPerSec, textureMemMB, peakProcessMemMB}` — plus a human-readable markdown summary. Schema shared with **SCR-046** via E06-D02.
- Runner ergonomics: `pnpm bench --scenario=B5 --runtime=electron --reps=3 --seed=…`, with a machine-descriptor block captured automatically (CPU, GPU, driver, OS build, WebView2 version where applicable).

## Out of scope
- Any production engine code; the harness renders whatever scene the K02/K03/K04 prototypes provide behind a tiny scene interface.
- CI *gating*: per `30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 the harness is committed and runnable with numbers recorded, but **not yet a required check** in R0. Wiring it as a gate belongs to E11.
- Backend load testing (k6/Locust) — that is E07/E08 territory.
- Real Bybit data or any network access during a run.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Fixtures are byte-reproducible
  Given seed 20260928 and the fixture generator
  When the generator runs twice on two different machines
  Then both outputs hash identically
  And the hash is asserted by a unit test that fails loudly if the generator's behaviour ever drifts

Scenario: A run reports per-stage attribution, not just a total
  Given the B5 combined scenario runs for 20 s
  When the JSON report is written
  Then it contains p50/p95/p99 overall and a perStageMs entry for each of the nine stages named in docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3
  And the stage costs sum to within 10 % of the measured frame time, with the residual reported as "unattributed"

Scenario: Statistical rules are enforced by the tool, not by discipline
  Given a run is requested with fewer than 3 repetitions
  When the report is generated
  Then it is marked "not admissible for ADR evidence" in the JSON and the markdown summary
  And the default repetition count is 3

Scenario: The machine is always identified
  Given any run on any runtime
  When the report is written
  Then CPU, GPU, driver version, OS build and (for Tauri) the exact WebView2 runtime version are captured automatically
  And a run missing any of these fields fails rather than reporting anonymous numbers

Scenario: The harness does not perturb what it measures
  Given instrumentation is enabled
  When the same scenario is run with instrumentation disabled
  Then the difference in p95 frame time is <= 3 %, or the overhead is documented and subtracted consistently
```

## Technical notes / design
- Scene interface kept deliberately minimal so prototype scenes are swappable: `interface BenchScene { init(gl, fixture): Promise<void>; step(t: number, input: DriverEvent | null): void; stats(): FrameStats; dispose(): void }`.
- Driver events are synthesised deterministically from a script (time-parameterised, not frame-parameterised) so a slow machine executes the same logical motion as a fast one — otherwise a slow runtime silently gets an easier test.
- Warm-up: discard the first 2 s of every run (shader compilation, atlas generation, JIT) and report cold-init separately as B9; conflating them would slander every runtime equally but uselessly.
- GPU memory is an estimate from tracked allocations (WebGL exposes no true figure); label it as an estimate everywhere, including in the SCR-046 vocabulary.
- Peak process memory via `performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory()` where available, falling back to the Electron/Tauri host process metrics; state which source produced the figure in the report.
- Zero allocation in the frame path is a design rule of the engine (`26-…` §3.2 rule 4); the harness samples an allocation counter so K02/K03/K04 can be checked against it.
- Flag set for headless Chromium must be pinned and printed in the report — GPU flags change results materially and an unpinned flag set makes runs incomparable across weeks.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: fixture determinism (hash equality across runs and platforms); tick-integer price invariants (no float dollars anywhere in the fixture); driver-script time-parameterisation (same logical motion at 30 fps and 144 fps); report-schema validation; "< 3 reps -> not admissible" flag; missing-machine-descriptor -> failure.
- **Integration**: full B5 run against a stub scene producing known synthetic frame times, asserting the reported p50/p95/p99 match the injected distribution within tolerance (this validates the statistics, not the GPU).
- **Contract**: report JSON validated against the schema shared with E06-D02's counter vocabulary.
- Coverage: >= 85 % on the merged harness + generator (engine-package threshold). Prototype scenes are exempt as throwaway code.
- Fixtures: seeds are checked into the repo; generated artefacts are not (they are reproducible by definition).

## Security notes
- Supply chain is the live threat (STRIDE **T**ampering, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5 and §12): the harness pulls Playwright, an Electron build and, for the Tauri arm, a Rust toolchain. All must be pinned by exact version with lockfile entries, and go through the same Dependabot/npm-audit/pip-audit gates as production code. Reviewed by **E06-X02**.
- The harness performs no network I/O at run time; assert this (no fetch/XHR/WS during a benchmark run) so a fixture can never be silently sourced from the internet.
- No credentials, no exchange connectivity, no PII. Data classification: none.

## Accessibility notes
The harness itself is a developer tool with no user surface (N/A for WCAG conformance), but it must expose the **DOM-mirror sync** stage as a first-class measured stage so the a11y layer's cost is never invisible — required by E06-D03 and by the 1 ms allocation in `06-…` §4.3.

## Performance notes
Harness overhead <= 3 % of measured p95 (see acceptance criteria). Establishes the baselines later governed by the <= 5 % regression gate (`06-…` §7.4), including the baseline-update policy that baselines move only via a reviewed PR.

## Observability
Defines the run-report JSON that is the Epic's primary evidence artefact, and the counter vocabulary mirrored by SCR-046. Reports are committed as artefacts alongside the M0 report so future engine work can diff against M0 numbers.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Harness and fixture generator merged to `main` (this part is **not** throwaway) with >= 85 % coverage.
- [ ] `pnpm bench` documented in the package README with the pinned flag set.
- [ ] Determinism test green in CI; schema contract test green.

title: Prototype scene A: 100k-bar model, visible-window draw and LOD ladder
body:
## Context
The first thing the custom engine must prove is the thing every charting library already does well, because if we cannot match chassis parity we should be using a chassis. `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md` is candid that the fully custom route adds "~4-8 weeks to reach chassis parity (pan/zoom momentum, axis decimation, multi-pane sync, crosshair, DPI correctness)" and makes milestone **M1 (chassis parity)** deliberately first so the riskiest unknown resolves early. M0's job is the cheaper precursor: demonstrate that a 100k-bar virtual model with visible-window draw and a working LOD ladder holds **B1** (<= 12 ms p95, <= 8 draw calls, continuous pan at 1000 px/s) and **B2** (<= 14 ms p95, <= 6 LOD changes over a 0.1 -> 50 px/bar zoom sweep, no flicker).

The subtlety that makes this worth measuring rather than assuming is in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.1: the 16.6 ms budget is a **per-frame visible-window** cost, not an "iterate 100k bars per frame" cost. Getting that wrong is the classic way a custom engine dies — and the L2 decimation rule (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6) adds a correctness requirement on top: per-pixel-column min/max preserving reduction, so price spikes never vanish when zoomed out. A fast engine that eats spikes is a broken engine.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Prototype scene A on branch `spike/e06-engine-m0`, implementing the `BenchScene` interface from E06-K01:
  - `BarStore`-shaped columnar model (`time: Float64Array`, OHLC/volume/delta as `Float32Array`, ring indices, capacity doubling) per `26-…` §3.3, holding 100k bars.
  - Visible-window slicing with a prefetch margin; off-window bars never touched by the render loop.
  - Instanced candle rendering (one quad, per-instance attributes) with pixel-snapping for hairlines, MSAA off, depth test off (`26-…` §3.4).
  - LOD ladder L0 full OHLC bodies+wicks / L1 bodies only / L2 min-max column strip, with the px-per-bar thresholds and +/-15 % hysteresis of §3.6.
  - Viewport math per §3.5: bar-index-space panning with `barSpacing` clamped to [0.05, 200] px, cursor-anchored zoom (world coordinate under the anchor invariant), momentum with exponential decay (tau = 120 ms, terminate below 0.02 px/ms).
  - Time and price axes with decimation, enough to be representative of real per-frame cost — this is not chrome, axis label layout is a measurable cost.
  - `priceOrigin` double-precision offset on the CPU, integer-tick prices, `time - viewportTimeOrigin` passed to the shader as float32 (§3.3 precision rule).
- Benchmarks wired: **B1**, **B2**, and **B9** (cold init to first frame with 100k bars, <= 900 ms).
- Correctness proof for L2 decimation: a test asserting the min/max-preserving reduction retains every spike present in the source data for a fixture containing deliberate single-bar extremes.
- Measured output feeding **E06-T01** (runtime matrix) and **E06-T02** (report).

## Out of scope
- Footprint cells and SDF text (**E06-K03**), heatmap (**E06-K04**).
- Multi-pane layout and sync, crosshair interaction polish, drawings, indicators, trading overlays — all M1+ production work in E11.
- Any production-quality API, React bindings, or option diffing. This is throwaway code and must be labelled as such in its README.
- Touch/pinch gestures (measured only if trivial; the reference surface is mouse/trackpad).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: B1 continuous pan holds the budget
  Given the 100k-bar seeded fixture loaded into the prototype
  When the scripted continuous pan at 1000 px/s runs for 20 s in headless Chromium
  Then p95 frame time is <= 12 ms and draw calls per frame are <= 8
  And per-stage attribution shows data-window recompute <= 2 ms and candle geometry update <= 2 ms per docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3

Scenario: B2 zoom sweep does not flicker between detail levels
  Given a wheel zoom sweep from 0.1 to 50 px/bar
  When the sweep runs
  Then p95 frame time is <= 14 ms
  And the number of LOD level changes over the whole sweep is <= 6, demonstrating the +/-15 % hysteresis band works

Scenario: Decimation never eats a spike
  Given a fixture containing isolated single-bar high/low extremes
  When the view is zoomed out far enough to engage L2 min-max column reduction
  Then every extreme is still present in the rendered column strip, verified by reading back the framebuffer or the emitted geometry
  And a regression test encodes this so the property cannot be optimised away later

Scenario: Only the visible window is processed
  Given 100k bars are loaded and ~300 are visible
  When a static frame is rendered
  Then the number of bars touched by the render loop is within the visible window plus the prefetch margin, asserted by an instrumentation counter
  And frame time does not scale measurably with total bar count (10k vs 100k differ by <= 10 % on a static frame)

Scenario: Cold init stays under budget
  Given a cold page load with the 100k-bar fixture
  When time-to-first-frame is measured
  Then it is <= 900 ms (B9), reported separately from steady-state numbers
```

## Technical notes / design
- Bar-space vs time-space: pan/zoom operate in bar-index space with a monotone index->time map; the scene exposes both `indexToScreen` and `timeToScreen` because the heatmap scene (K04) needs true time (§3.5). Getting this dual mapping right in M0 is what makes K04's alignment work rather than a fudge.
- Auto-scale recomputes only when the visible bar range changes, throttled to once per frame (§3.5) — measure it in the data-window stage, not hidden in draw.
- No allocation in the hot path (§3.2 rule 4): pool all per-frame structures; the harness's allocation counter must show zero GC-triggering allocations during a steady pan.
- Render-on-demand: with no data and no interaction the loop parks. Verify this is true, since a prototype that spins rAF forever will flatter nothing but will mislead the battery/idle discussion for E10.
- Axis decimation: label density chosen by available px per label with a nice-number ladder; label text uses the same text path that K03 builds if available, otherwise Canvas-2D overlay — state which was used, because it changes the text-stage cost attribution.

## Test plan
- **Unit** (on the harness-side helpers that survive): index<->screen transform round-trip; `barSpacing` clamping; LOD threshold selection including hysteresis boundaries (just inside/outside the dead band); min/max decimation correctness on spike fixtures; momentum decay integration is dt-based (same outcome at 30 and 144 fps).
- **Integration**: full B1/B2/B9 runs via the E06-K01 harness against the seeded fixture, 3 repetitions, medians of p95 compared to budget.
- **Visual**: golden-image capture at each LOD level so E11 inherits reference images (not gating in M0, but captured).
- **Perf**: B1, B2, B9 as above; static-frame scaling check (10k vs 100k bars).
- Coverage: throwaway prototype code is exempt (stated per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.2); helpers promoted into the harness carry >= 85 %.

## Security notes
No new surface beyond E06-K01's supply chain (STRIDE **T**ampering). No network I/O during a run; synthetic fixtures only; no credentials. Data classification: none. Shader code is authored in-repo, not fetched, so there is no remote-code path into the GPU pipeline.

## Accessibility notes
N/A for this scene in isolation — the a11y layer is measured in **E06-D03** against the combined scene. One constraint carried here: the LOD ladder must expose its current level as state that the accessible layer can read (US-CHART-001 requires "the aggregation level is indicated"), so the prototype exposes `currentLod` in `stats()` rather than keeping it internal.

## Performance notes
Budgets: **B1** p95 <= 12 ms, <= 8 draw calls; **B2** p95 <= 14 ms, <= 6 LOD changes; **B9** cold init <= 900 ms. Stage slices: data-window recompute <= 2 ms, candle geometry <= 2 ms, input handling <= 1 ms (`06-…` §4.3). US-CHART-001 NFR: >= 55 fps at 100k bars; US-CHART-006 NFR: input-to-pixel latency <= 1 frame.

## Observability
Scene reports `{visibleBars, barsTouched, currentLod, lodChanges, drawCalls, bufferBytesUploaded, allocationsInFramePath}` through `stats()` into the harness JSON; these become the SCR-046 counters (E06-D02) in production.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] B1, B2, B9 measured in headless Chromium with >= 3 reps; numbers recorded in the harness report format.
- [ ] Decimation spike-preservation test green.
- [ ] Visible-window-only processing proven by counter, not by inspection.
- [ ] Golden images captured per LOD level and handed to E11.
- [ ] Findings (what was hard, what surprised, what M1 must budget for) written up for the E06-T02 report.
- [ ] Prototype README states clearly that the code is throwaway and why.

title: Prototype scene B: SDF text atlas and 2,500-cell footprint density (B3)
body:
## Context
Dense per-cell text is the single largest CPU-side cost in the product and the flagged engineering risk: `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3 gives footprint cell text/geometry the largest slice of the frame budget (**<= 4 ms**), and `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` records CMP-184 FootprintSeries as "the highest-effort chassis piece per research — the single largest line item". No surveyed charting library renders it at all (`ADR-0002`), so this is precisely the capability the custom engine exists to provide. If it cannot be done at density, the custom-engine decision fails on its own terms.

`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.7 commits to a specific strategy — a runtime-generated **signed distance field** atlas (1024x1024, two-pass Felzenszwalb EDT, shelf-packed, cached in IndexedDB keyed by `(fontFamily, weight, hash(glyphSet))`), instanced glyph draws, per-cell glyph runs precomputed on data update rather than per frame, and <= 6 text draw calls per pane. It also records the alternative the spike must actually measure against: a **Canvas-2D glyph cache**. `26-…` §16 keeps the exact atlas size and glyph set open as item **O2**. This ticket closes the strategy question with numbers, not preference.

Benchmark **B3** is the gate: 2,500 visible cells with text, p95 <= 16 ms, text batching <= 2.0 ms, <= 2 text draw calls. Per §3.7's own arithmetic that is ~12,500 glyphs at 5 characters average.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Prototype scene B on `spike/e06-engine-m0`:
  - **SDF atlas pipeline**: glyph rasterisation from the design-system font (frozen glyph set from **E06-D01**), two-pass EDT to an 8-bit single-channel SDF, shelf packing into a 1024x1024 atlas, IndexedDB caching with the documented key, and a measured generation cost (§3.7 claims ~40 ms once per font/size-class).
  - **Instanced glyph rendering**: per-instance `vec2 posPx, vec2 sizePx, vec4 uvRect, vec4 colour`; fragment shader `alpha = smoothstep(0.5 - w, 0.5 + w, sdf)` with `w = fwidth(sdf)`; optional second-threshold outline pass for legibility over saturated cells (required if E06-D01 says so).
  - **FootprintStore**-shaped data (parallel `barIndex: Uint32Array`, `priceLevel: Int32Array`, `bidVol/askVol: Float32Array`, `tradeCount: Uint16Array`, `offsets` prefix sums) per §3.3, with `upsertFootprintCells` returning affected ranges for partial `bufferSubData`.
  - **Per-cell glyph-run caching**: values formatted to strings on data update, glyph runs cached alongside the cell; format change invalidates only the run cache.
  - LOD ladder L0/L1/L2/L3 using the thresholds from **E06-D01**, including the non-colour encodings (delta glyph, imbalance outline, estimated-data hatch).
  - **Comparison arm**: the same scene rendered with a Canvas-2D glyph cache, measured identically, so the SDF choice is evidence-backed.
- Benchmark **B3** wired and run; atlas generation cost and cached-load cost (<= 5 ms from cache, per B9's secondary gate) measured.
- Answer to open item **O2**: final atlas dimensions, glyph set and size-class strategy, recorded as an update to `26-…` §16.
- Components exercised: **CMP-109 FootprintCell**, **CMP-184 FootprintSeries**.
- Stories informed: **US-CHART-001**, **US-CHART-003**, **US-CHART-008**.

## Out of scope
- Imbalance detection logic, Deep-Stats rows, stacked-imbalance semantics — order-flow *computation* is backend work (FP/DS domains, later epics); this scene renders precomputed synthetic cells.
- Cell tooltips, pick-based cell detail drawers, the CMP-109 per-cell DOM surrogate (measured structurally in **E06-D03**).
- Candles and axes (**E06-K02**) and heatmap (**E06-K04**), except as composited in the combined scene owned by **E06-T01**.
- Production-quality text layout: bidi, complex scripts, ligatures. The glyph set is numeric plus Latin labels (E06-D01), which is the real product requirement.

### Scope trim (21-point roadmap budget)
The Canvas-2D glyph-cache arm is a **single spot-check configuration** at B3 density, not a second production-grade text renderer. It exists only to answer "is the SDF atlas clearly better, clearly worse, or within noise". If the spot check lands within noise, that is recorded as a finding and the full comparison is deferred to **E11 M3** rather than extending the M0 timebox.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: B3 holds at product density
  Given 2,500 visible footprint cells each rendering two numbers at the L0 threshold set by E06-D01
  When the B3 scenario runs for 20 s in headless Chromium with 3 repetitions
  Then the median p95 frame time is <= 16 ms
  And text batching costs <= 2.0 ms per frame with <= 2 text draw calls

Scenario: SDF beats or loses to Canvas-2D on evidence
  Given both the SDF atlas arm and the Canvas-2D glyph-cache arm render the identical scene
  When both are measured under the same conditions and repetitions
  Then a comparison table reports p95 frame time, text-stage ms, draw calls and memory for each
  And 26-chart-engine-design.md §3.7's text strategy is confirmed or amended to match the winner

Scenario: Atlas generation is paid once, not per launch
  Given a cold first launch with an empty IndexedDB
  When the atlas is generated
  Then generation cost is measured and reported (target ~40 ms per font/size-class)
  And on a second launch the atlas loads from cache in <= 5 ms, keyed by (fontFamily, weight, hash(glyphSet))

Scenario: Text stays legible over saturated cells
  Given the most saturated cell background in the dark theme
  When cell numbers are rendered at the L0 size
  Then measured contrast is >= 4.5:1 per docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §5, using the outline pass if E06-D01 requires it
  And the cost of the outline pass is reported separately so its budget impact is explicit

Scenario: Degradation sheds text, not correctness
  Given pixels-per-bar falls below the L1 threshold
  When the LOD ladder degrades to L2 (coloured cells, no text)
  Then no cell disappears and no value is misrepresented — only text is withheld
  And the transition is hysteretic, with no flicker over a slow zoom

Scenario: Formatting changes do not cost a frame
  Given the number format switches from full to compact (1.2K)
  When the change is applied
  Then only the glyph-run cache is invalidated, not the cell data
  And the reformatting cost is reported and does not exceed one frame's data-mutation budget of 4 ms, spilling to subsequent frames if needed
```

## Technical notes / design
- Batching rule from §3.7: all cell text in a pane is one draw call; axis labels a second; drawing labels a third; target <= 6 text draw calls per pane per frame. B3's gate of <= 2 text draw calls applies to the footprint scene specifically.
- Precompute formatting on data update, never per frame — this is the difference between hitting and missing the 4 ms stage budget.
- The `fwidth`-based smoothstep gives crisp text at any scale; verify at DPR 1.0/1.5/2.0 since the design-system font's stem widths behave differently at fractional DPRs.
- Shelf packing must be deterministic so the atlas is reproducible; record the packing order hash in the report.
- Memory: atlas is 1024x1024x1 byte = 1 MB; report actual GPU texture memory including any driver padding.
- If the glyph count at L0 exceeds what one instanced draw can carry comfortably, chunk by fixed instance budget and report the chunk count — silently exceeding the draw-call gate is a failure, not an implementation detail.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: EDT correctness against a reference implementation on known shapes; shelf packer determinism and no-overlap invariant; glyph-run cache invalidation on format change only; `offsets` prefix-sum correctness for `FootprintStore`; LOD threshold selection at hysteresis boundaries.
- **Integration**: B3 via the harness, 3 reps, both arms (SDF and Canvas-2D); atlas cold-generate vs cached-load timing.
- **Visual**: golden images per LOD level at DPR 1.0 and 2.0, handed to E11's M3.
- **A11y-adjacent**: contrast measurement on rendered output (automated sampling of text pixels against cell background).
- Coverage: prototype exempt; any helper promoted to the harness carries >= 85 %.

## Security notes
- Font handling is the notable surface: the atlas is generated at runtime from the design-system font, so the font must be a pinned, vendored asset, not fetched from a third-party CDN (STRIDE **T**ampering, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5/§6). Record this as a constraint for E11.
- IndexedDB caching stores only glyph bitmaps keyed by a font hash — no user data, no PII; the key must not incorporate anything user-identifying.
- No network I/O during a benchmark run. Data classification: none (synthetic cells).

## Accessibility notes
- The non-colour encodings from **E06-D01** (delta glyph, imbalance outline, estimated hatch) are implemented in this scene precisely so their rendering cost is inside the measured budget rather than discovered later (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §4).
- Contrast >= 4.5:1 for cell text over its own background is an acceptance criterion here, not a later fix (§5).
- Per-cell DOM surrogates (CMP-109's `aria-label` composition and cell-to-cell arrow navigation) are structurally measured in **E06-D03**; this ticket must expose cell values through `stats()`/a data accessor so that measurement is possible.

## Performance notes
Budgets: **B3** p95 <= 16 ms, text batching <= 2.0 ms, <= 2 text draw calls; stage slice for footprint text/geometry <= 4 ms (`06-…` §4.3); atlas from cache <= 5 ms (B9 secondary). Text density degradation is the *second* lever in the degradation ladder (`06-…` §4.4), after heatmap cadence — so this scene must also demonstrate that shedding text actually recovers the budget.

## Observability
Scene reports `{visibleCells, glyphCount, textDrawCalls, textBatchMs, outlinePassMs, atlasGenMs, atlasCacheHit, atlasTextureBytes}` into the harness JSON; `glyphCount` and `textBatchMs` become SCR-046 counters via E06-D02.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] B3 measured (SDF and Canvas-2D arms) with >= 3 reps; comparison table produced.
- [ ] Open item **O2** closed: atlas size, glyph set and size-class strategy recorded in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §16.

- [ ] Golden images per LOD captured for E11.
- [ ] Findings written up for E06-T02, explicitly stating what M3 must budget.
- [ ] Reviewed by the chart-engine owner; design reviewer confirms rendered output matches E06-D01's spec.

title: Prototype scene C: 200-depth heatmap texture ring, 4h trail and 30-min soak
body:
## Context
The DOM liquidity heatmap is the surface that decides the **Electron vs Tauri** question. `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0011-electron-vs-tauri.md` says so plainly: "Tauri's WebView2 behaviour under sustained 100 ms heatmap texture updates is unverified, and it varies by OS-provided WebView version". Three of ADR-0011's five binding criteria are about this scene specifically — p95 within 10 % of Electron for B5, no frame-time outliers above 33 ms during a 30-minute soak that are absent under Electron, and no progressive degradation of `texSubImage2D` streaming at 10 Hz over 30 minutes.

The technique under test is the rolling-texture ring of `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.8: quantise each column to R16F, upload **one 1 x rows texture column** (512 x 2 bytes = 1 KB) per update regardless of trail length, advance a ring cursor mod 2048, draw one or two textured quads, and colour through a 256x1 LUT so a theme change is a single texture update. Constant upload cost independent of history is "the entire reason for the texture approach" — and it is exactly the property a WebView might fail to sustain.

Longer trails roll into a **coarse ring** (1 column per second instead of per 100 ms), giving 4 h+ of history at a tenth of the memory. Whether that coarse resolution should be 1 s or 2 s is open item **O3**, assigned for resolution from the soak.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Prototype scene C on `spike/e06-engine-m0`:
  - **Fine ring**: R16F texture, width 2048 columns, height 512 price rows, `writeCol` cursor, `colTime: Float64Array(2048)` for time mapping, `priceOrigin`/`priceStep` in integer ticks (`26-…` §3.3/§3.8). Memory target ~2 MB.
  - **Coarse ring**: 14,400 columns x 512 rows (~14 MB) for 4 h+ of history, with the shader selecting source by column age; both 1 s and 2 s candidate resolutions measured to close **O3**.
  - **Streaming**: `texSubImage2D(x = writeCol, w = 1, h = rows)` at 10 Hz from the seeded heatmap fixture; ring wrap drawn as two sub-quads.
  - **Colour**: 256x1 LUT texture using the ramp delivered by **E06-D02** (green = bid, red = ask per owner decision #10, configurable); theme switch implemented as a LUT swap and its cost measured to prove the one-texture-update claim. Log and linear intensity mappings and the age-decay curve as specified.
  - **Price-origin shifting**: when the market moves outside the row window, shift `priceOrigin` and re-upload only newly exposed rows (a vertical scroll of the ring) — never the whole texture. This path must be exercised by the fixture, since it is the easy thing to get wrong and the expensive thing to get wrong in production.
  - **Alignment** with the price scale and with scene A's time mapping (`timeToScreen`), so panning costs nothing extra.
  - DPR capped at 2 for the heatmap layer to bound texture cost (`26-…` §3.4).
- Benchmarks wired: **B4** (100 ms columns, 4 h trail, panning: p95 <= 10 ms, upload <= 12 KB/s, texture memory <= 20 MB) and **B10** (30-minute memory/streaming soak: peak <= 600 MB, no monotonic growth, no outliers > 33 ms).
- Capability probe results recorded: `EXT_color_buffer_float`, `R16F` render/sample support, `OES_texture_float_linear`, instancing, `OffscreenCanvas` in a worker — these are ADR-0011 criterion 4 verbatim.
- Components exercised: **CMP-193 HeatmapOverlay** (engine mount point, render/upload performance contract), **CMP-113 HeatmapLegend**.
- Stories informed: **US-CHART-001**, **US-CHART-006**; the DOM-domain heatmap stories consume this engine capability later.

## Out of scope
- Real order-book reconstruction, L2 delta application, iceberg/stop-run estimation — backend order-flow work in later epics; this scene consumes synthetic pre-aggregated columns.
- The DOM ladder UI (SCR-050 and the DOM domain screens).
- Final colour-blind-safe palette selection (open item **O5**, assigned to the M8 a11y pass); only E06-D02's candidate is exercised.
- Multi-symbol heatmaps and the per-symbol memory multiplication question beyond reporting per-symbol figures.

### Scope trim (21-point roadmap budget)
Measured at the 4 h trail and 30-minute soak required by benchmarks **B4** and **B10** only. Longer trails, multi-symbol heatmaps and coarse-ring resolution tuning (open item **O3**) are recorded as observations and deferred to **E11 M4**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: B4 holds with a 4-hour trail while panning
  Given the fine ring plus coarse ring holding a 4 h trail and columns arriving at 10 Hz
  When the B4 scenario runs for 20 s with panning, 3 repetitions
  Then median p95 frame time is <= 10 ms
  And uploaded bytes are <= 12 KB/s and total heatmap texture memory is <= 20 MB

Scenario: Upload cost is constant in trail length
  Given trails of 5 minutes, 1 hour and 4 hours
  When each is measured under identical column cadence
  Then uploaded bytes per second are equal within measurement noise across all three
  And frame time does not increase with trail length, proving the ring design rather than assuming it

Scenario: 30-minute soak shows no progressive degradation
  Given the B10 soak running the heatmap at 10 Hz for 30 minutes
  When frame times and process memory are sampled throughout
  Then peak memory is <= 600 MB with no monotonic growth beyond the documented steady-state variance band
  And there are no frame-time outliers above 33 ms, recorded per runtime so ADR-0011 criteria 2 and 3 can be evaluated

Scenario: Price-origin shift re-uploads only new rows
  Given the market moves outside the current row window
  When priceOrigin shifts
  Then only the newly exposed rows are uploaded, asserted by an instrumentation counter of uploaded bytes for that frame
  And the frame containing the shift does not exceed the frame budget

Scenario: Theme change is a LUT swap
  Given the bid/ask colour convention is switched
  When the change is applied
  Then exactly one 256x1 texture upload occurs and no heatmap data is re-uploaded
  And the switch completes within a single frame

Scenario: Capability gaps degrade rather than break
  Given a runtime where EXT_color_buffer_float or R16F sampling is unavailable
  When the capability probe runs
  Then the scene selects a reduced or degraded-2d profile and still renders correct (if coarser) output
  And the probe result is recorded in the run report for ADR-0011 criterion 4
```

## Technical notes / design
- Quantisation: normalise each column by column max or a global scale (both measured — the choice changes how spikes read and is a product question worth an explicit answer in the report).
- Column aggregation when more than one column maps to a pixel uses **max** of columns, preserving liquidity spikes (`26-…` §3.6) — same correctness principle as candle min/max decimation.
- The 100 ms cadence is a **visual refresh** cadence decoupled from message cadence (`06-…` §4.2): deltas are coalesced and sampled at 10 Hz, so a message-rate spike must not translate 1:1 into upload spikes. Demonstrate this by driving the fixture at 5x message rate and confirming upload bytes stay flat.
- Degradation lever #1 in `06-…` §4.4 is reducing heatmap cadence from 100 ms toward 250 ms; implement and measure it so the ladder is evidence-backed.
- Coarse-ring selection by column age happens in the shader; the boundary must be exact or a visible seam appears at the transition — check it in a golden image.
- Report memory per symbol (fine + coarse) so the capacity discussion for 10 recorded symbols (`06-…` §10) is grounded.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: ring cursor wrap arithmetic (including the two-sub-quad draw case); `colTime` mapping monotonicity; price-origin shift computing exactly the newly exposed row range; LUT generation from the E06-D02 ramp matching legend tick values; coarse/fine selection boundary by age.
- **Integration**: B4 and B10 via the harness; constant-upload-vs-trail-length experiment; 5x message-rate coalescing experiment; theme-swap cost.
- **Chaos** (per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §9): simulate a WebGL **context loss** mid-soak and verify the documented recovery (stop loop, invalidate GPU resources, rebuild from the data model, one-frame flash, no data loss — `26-…` §3.4). This is the cheapest place to prove context-loss recovery works at all.
