title: Run the measurement matrix across Chromium, Electron and Tauri/WebView2
body:
## Context
The three prototype scenes exist; this ticket turns them into the evidence table that both ADRs consume. `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §7.1 names the three runtimes: headless Chromium (primary CI target), Electron (release-representative), and Tauri/WebView2 **during the engine spike only**. `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0011-electron-vs-tauri.md` lists five binding criteria, all of which are decided by numbers produced here, and sets the deadline at the end of Sprint 03 — so the matrix must complete inside Sprint 02 to leave room for the decision and any re-runs.

The reason this is a separate ticket rather than a step inside each scene spike is that cross-runtime comparison has its own discipline: identical fixtures, identical seeds, identical driver scripts, the same machine, versions of everything captured, and enough repetitions that a 10 % criterion (ADR-0011 criterion 1) means something. Folding it into the scene work invites each scene being measured slightly differently, which would make the comparison worthless precisely where it matters most.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Runtime targets built and pinned:
  - **Headless Chromium** via Playwright with the pinned GPU flag set from E06-K01.
  - **Electron** harness shell with `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `sandbox: true` and the GPU flags under evaluation (the hardening baseline from **E06-X01**; also the input to E10's shell configuration).
  - **Tauri v2 / WebView2** harness shell, with the exact WebView2 runtime version recorded — the whole point of the arm is that this version is OS-updated and results are only meaningful when versioned.
- Full matrix executed: scenarios **B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B7, B9, B10** x 3 runtimes, >= 3 repetitions each (soaks once per runtime), medians of p95 per `06-…` §7.4.
- **B5 combined scene** assembled here from scenes A+B+C plus 3 synthetic indicator series and 50 order lines — this is the scene R0 exit criterion 4 is stated against (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.3), so its composition is documented precisely and its gates are p95 <= 16.7 ms and <= 40 draw calls.
- **B7 live update storm** (20 data messages/s x 6 stores, decode p95 <= 4 ms, zero dropped messages) exercising the worker + `OffscreenCanvas` path and the `RunMode.inline` fallback for runtimes lacking `OffscreenCanvas`.
- ADR-0011 criteria evaluated one by one with the measured figure and a pass/fail, including criterion 5 (shell responsibility parity) whose checklist comes from **E06-X01**.
- Machine descriptor and full version manifest per run (CPU, GPU, driver, OS build, Electron version, Chromium version, Tauri version, WebView2 version, Node version, flag set).
- Raw JSON artefacts committed alongside the report.

## Out of scope
- Writing the report or the ADRs (**E06-T02**, **E06-T03**).
- Optimising the scenes: if a budget is missed, this ticket records it; whether to spend timebox on optimisation is an Architect call made against the M0 timebox, and any optimisation lands in the scene tickets.
- Measuring on secondary hardware beyond the reference machine and the one compatibility-sweep machine from **E06-Q02**.
- Standing CI runs of the Tauri arm — explicitly not a standing CI target once the decision is finalised (`06-…` §7.1).

### Scope trim (21-point roadmap budget)
The binding matrix legs are **Electron** and **Tauri v2 / WebView2** — ADR-0011 turns on their difference and R0 exit criterion 4 is stated in Electron. **Headless Chromium** is retained as a one-configuration baseline smoke arm (useful for attributing a regression to the shell vs the engine), not as a full leg.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The matrix is complete and comparable
  Given eight scenarios and three runtimes
  When the matrix has run
  Then every cell has a median-of-p95 result from >= 3 repetitions, or a documented reason it could not run (e.g. missing WebGL2 capability)
  And every run used the same seed, fixture and driver script, asserted by the seed and fixture hash recorded in each report

Scenario: R0 exit criterion 4 is answered unambiguously
  Given the B5 combined scene in Electron on the reference machine
  When results are tabulated
  Then p50 and p95 frame times are stated against the >= 60 fps p50 / >= 55 fps p95 bar from docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md §4.3
  And the verdict is stated as pass or fail without hedging, with per-stage attribution showing where the time went

Scenario: ADR-0011 criterion 1 is decided on a like-for-like comparison
  Given B5 p95 in WebView2 and in Electron on the same machine in the same session
  When the difference is computed
  Then it is reported as a percentage against the 10 % threshold
  And the WebView2 runtime version is recorded next to the figure

Scenario: Soak outliers are attributed to a runtime, not to noise
  Given the 30-minute B10 soak in each runtime
  When frame-time outliers above 33 ms are counted
  Then outliers present in WebView2 but absent in Electron are identified as such per ADR-0011 criterion 2
  And any outlier present in all runtimes is investigated as an engine issue rather than a shell issue

Scenario: A capability gap is a result, not a blocker
  Given a runtime that lacks EXT_color_buffer_float, R16F sampling, instancing or OffscreenCanvas in a worker
  When the capability probe runs
  Then the gap is recorded against ADR-0011 criterion 4
  And the affected scenarios run in the reduced or degraded-2d profile with results labelled accordingly, rather than being omitted
```

## Technical notes / design
- Same machine, same session, alternating runtimes (A/B/A ordering) to cancel thermal drift — a sequential "all Electron then all Tauri" schedule would let a warm machine slander the second runtime.
- Close everything else on the reference machine; record background load. Note that the backend stack (WSL, Docker, QuestDB, Postgres) is the realistic co-tenant per ADR-0011's memory argument, so run one **co-tenancy variant** of B5 with the dev stack running, and report resident memory for each shell — this is the evidence for ADR-0011's "roughly 100-150 MB higher than Tauri" claim.
- `OffscreenCanvas` availability differs across WebViews; where absent, run `RunMode.inline` and label the result, because the inline mode's numbers are not comparable to worker-mode numbers and must never be averaged together.
- Electron GPU flags are themselves a variable; measure the default flag set and the tuned set, and hand the winner to **E10** as the recommended configuration.
- Tauri arm needs a minimal Rust host; keep it to the smallest possible shell that can load the harness page and expose the same driver hooks, to avoid measuring our Rust code instead of WebView2.

## Test plan
- The matrix *is* the test. Its own validity is checked by **E06-Q01** (methodology validation) and its cross-machine reproducibility by **E06-Q02** (compat sweep).
- Sanity gate before accepting results: run the same scenario twice in the same runtime and confirm the two medians of p95 agree within the documented noise band; if they do not, the matrix is not admissible and the noise source must be found first.
- Contract: every emitted report validates against the E06-K01 JSON schema.

## Security notes
- The Electron harness shell must already carry the mandatory hardening from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` — `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `sandbox: true`, strict CSP, allow-list preload, navigation and `window.open` blocked — because these settings have measurable performance implications and measuring an unhardened shell would produce numbers we can never ship against (STRIDE **E**levation of privilege). Checklist supplied by **E06-X01**.
- The Tauri arm introduces a Rust toolchain and crate dependencies: pinned, lockfile-committed, and scanned (**E06-X02**).
- No network access during runs; no credentials; synthetic data only. Data classification: none.

## Accessibility notes
The DOM-mirror stage from **E06-D03** is included in the matrix runs so its cost is measured in all three runtimes, not just Chromium — a WebView with slower DOM performance would hit the a11y layer hardest, and that must be part of the shell decision rather than a later surprise.

## Performance notes
All budgets from `26-chart-engine-design.md` §13 (B1-B10) and the stage allocations of `06-…` §4.3 apply. The decisive figures are B5 in Electron (R0 exit criterion 4) and B5/B10 in WebView2 vs Electron (ADR-0011 criteria 1-3).

## Observability
Produces the complete set of run-report JSON artefacts that become the project's first performance baselines, subject afterwards to the baseline-update policy in `06-…` §7.4 (baselines move only via a reviewed PR with rationale).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All matrix cells executed or explicitly justified as not-runnable.
- [ ] Raw JSON artefacts committed; version manifest complete for every run.
- [ ] Co-tenancy variant and resident-memory comparison recorded.
- [ ] ADR-0011 criteria 1-5 each carry a measured figure and a pass/fail.

- [ ] Recommended Electron GPU flag set handed to **E10**.
- [ ] Noise-band sanity gate passed before results were accepted.
- [ ] Architect review of the matrix before it is used as ADR evidence.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E06-K02, E06-K03, E06-K04` — the three scenes.

- Blocks **E06-T02**.

title: Write the M0 findings report and commit the CI benchmark harness job
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.2 requires a Spike to answer its questions "with recorded evidence (benchmark numbers, prototype repo/branch link, comparison table)" and to record the decision as an ADR. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 adds a specific R0 quality-gate row: "E06 benchmark harness committed and runnable in CI (numbers recorded, not yet gating)". This ticket produces both — the written M0 report that ADR-0002 and ADR-0011 cite as their validation, and the CI job that keeps the numbers alive after the spike ends.

The report matters beyond the two decisions. Everything E11 builds over ten sprints is sized against these numbers, and `26-chart-engine-design.md` §15's milestone estimates are only credible if M0's findings say what M1-M8 must budget. A report that just says "it was fast enough" would satisfy the letter of the gate and waste the spike.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **M0 findings report** at `docs/plan/28-m0-engine-spike-report.md` (new file, linked from ADR-0002, ADR-0011 and `26-chart-engine-design.md` §15), containing:
  - Executive verdict: custom engine go/no-go against R0 exit criterion 4; Electron vs Tauri recommendation against ADR-0011's five criteria.
  - Full results matrix: B1-B10 x 3 runtimes, medians of p95 from >= 3 repetitions, with p50/p95/p99 and per-stage attribution against `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3.
  - Machine and version manifest, including the WebView2 runtime version, so the results are reproducible and their shelf life is understood.
  - Text-strategy comparison (SDF atlas vs Canvas-2D glyph cache) from **E06-K03**, with the decision and its rationale.
  - Heatmap findings from **E06-K04**: constant-upload proof, coarse-ring resolution choice (open item **O3**), per-symbol memory, context-loss recovery evidence.
  - A11y cost section from **E06-D03**: measured DOM-mirror sync cost against its 1 ms allocation, announcement cadence decision, LOD/mirror parity rule.
  - Compatibility findings from **E06-Q02**: which GPU/driver combinations were swept, what degraded, what the `degraded-2d` profile actually delivers.
  - **What M1-M8 must budget**: a section translating findings into concrete guidance per milestone in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §15, so E11's tickets inherit evidence rather than re-deriving it.
  - Residual unknowns explicitly listed as open items with owners, rather than being quietly omitted.
- **CI job**: benchmark harness wired into the pipeline (GitHub Actions, per `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0013-ci-pipeline.md` and E03's workflow set) on a dedicated runner — headless Chromium per PR touching `packages/chart-engine`, Electron nightly (startup cost makes per-PR impractical, per `06-…` §7.1). **Recording only, not gating**, with baselines committed and the baseline-update policy of `06-…` §7.4 documented in the package README.
- Follow-up tickets filed against **E11** (per-milestone guidance) and **E10** (recommended GPU flag set, shell hardening settings), each linking the report so implementers do not re-derive findings — required by DoD §5.2.
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated: **R2** and **R8** re-scored with evidence; **R10** key-person mitigation noted (the report is the transferable artefact).

## Out of scope
- The ADR edits themselves (**E06-T03**) — this ticket supplies the evidence they cite.
- Making the benchmarks a required check: that is E11's job once the engine is real and baselines are meaningful (`30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 says "not yet gating" for R0).
- Backend/API load-testing CI (E03/E07 territory).
- Re-running the matrix: if the report reveals a gap, a re-run is a change to E06-T01, not a silent extension here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The report is self-sufficient evidence
  Given a reader who was not involved in the spike
  When they read docs/plan/28-m0-engine-spike-report.md
  Then they can state the verdict on the custom engine and on the shell choice, see the numbers behind each, and identify the machine and software versions that produced them
  And every claim in the executive verdict traces to a row in the results matrix

Scenario: The CI job runs and records without blocking
  Given a PR touching packages/chart-engine
  When CI runs
  Then the headless Chromium benchmark job executes and publishes its report artefact
  And a regression does not fail the build in R0, but is visible as a published comparison against the committed baseline

Scenario: Nightly Electron coverage exists
  Given the nightly schedule
  When the Electron benchmark variant runs
  Then its results are published and compared to the Electron baseline
  And a failure to run is itself surfaced, rather than silently producing no data

Scenario: Follow-ups exist before the Epic closes
  Given the report's "what M1-M8 must budget" section
  When the Epic is reviewed for closure
  Then follow-up tickets exist against E11 and E10 citing specific report sections
  And the risk register reflects the re-scored R2 and R8

Scenario: Unknowns are stated, not hidden
  Given questions the spike could not answer inside its timebox
  When the report is finalised
  Then each is listed as a named open item with an owner and a resolution path, consistent with 26-chart-engine-design.md §16
```

## Technical notes / design
- Report structure follows the ADR validation sections it feeds, so ADR-0002's "Validation" and ADR-0011's "Validation" can cite specific headings rather than the document as a whole.
- Numbers in the report are generated from the committed JSON artefacts by a small script, not transcribed by hand — transcription errors in an ADR's evidence base are unacceptable and easily avoided.
- CI runner must be a dedicated machine with a stable GPU and a pinned flag set (`26-…` §13); a shared runner produces noise that would make even non-gating numbers misleading. Document the runner's specification in the report's manifest section.
- Baselines are committed as JSON alongside the harness; the update policy (baselines move forward only via a reviewed PR with rationale) is documented where an engineer will actually read it — the package README, not only the standards doc.
- Repetition and median-of-p95 rules from `06-…` §7.4 are enforced by the harness (E06-K01), so the CI job inherits them rather than restating them.

## Test plan
- **Contract**: the report-generation script validates every input artefact against the E06-K01 JSON schema and fails on a missing machine descriptor or a sub-3-repetition run marked inadmissible.
- **Integration**: CI job verified by a deliberate dry run on a branch, confirming artefact publication and baseline comparison output.
- **Review**: report reviewed by the Architect, the chart-engine lead and a second engineer who did not run the measurements (reproducibility reviewer from **E06-Q01**).
- Coverage: report-generation script carries the package threshold (>= 85 %).

title: Validate benchmark methodology and reproducibility before ADR evidence use
body:
## Context
This Epic's output is not software — it is evidence that two ADRs and an entire ten-sprint engine plan rest on. Evidence that cannot be reproduced is not evidence. `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §7.4 sets the statistical rules (>= 3 repetitions, compare medians of p95, never a single noisy sample) precisely because CI-runner and workstation noise produce false verdicts, and ADR-0011's criterion 1 is a **10 % difference** — a threshold small enough that sloppy methodology could decide the shell question by accident.

There is also a key-person dimension. `ADR-0002` names graphics-capable headcount as a bus-factor concern (risk **R10**), mitigated by "pairing on the engine squad, mandatory design docs per milestone, and CI benchmarks that make regressions visible to anyone". A benchmark only makes regressions visible to anyone if someone other than its author can run it and get the same answer. This ticket is QA's independent verification that the instrument is sound before anybody reads its dial.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Methodology review** of the E06-K01 harness against `06-…` §7.1-§7.4, written up as a findings list with severities:
  - warm-up handling (first 2 s discarded; cold-init reported separately as B9);
  - driver scripts are time-parameterised, not frame-parameterised, so a slow runtime is not given an easier test;
  - repetition and median-of-p95 enforcement, and the "< 3 reps -> not admissible" marking;
  - instrumentation overhead <= 3 % of measured p95, verified by an instrumented/uninstrumented A/B;
  - stage attribution sums to within 10 % of measured frame time with the residual reported as "unattributed";
  - no network I/O during a run; fixture hash and seed recorded in every report.
- **Independent reproduction**: a second engineer (not the harness author) runs B1, B3, B4 and B5 on a **second machine of the same reference class**, from a clean checkout, following only the written instructions. The measured cross-machine delta becomes the project's documented **noise band**, cited whenever two numbers are compared.
- **Documentation walkthrough**: the package README is followed literally; every point where the reproducer had to guess, ask or improvise is filed as a defect against E06-K01. A benchmark whose operation is tribal knowledge fails this ticket.
- **Negative tests** of the harness's own guards: a run with 2 repetitions must be marked inadmissible; a run missing the GPU/driver/OS descriptor must fail; a run whose fixture hash differs from the recorded seed must fail loudly rather than proceed.
- **Black-box test plan** for the Epic (per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11), covering the acceptance criteria of K02/K03/K04 that are observable without reading engine internals: spike preservation at L2, no LOD flicker across a slow zoom, footprint text legibility at the chosen threshold, heatmap constant-upload behaviour, theme-swap cost, context-loss recovery.
- **QA sign-off gate**: E06-T02 may not publish results as ADR evidence until this ticket passes.

## Out of scope
- Judging the engine's performance — QA validates the instrument and the process, not the verdict.
- GPU/driver compatibility sweeping across diverse hardware (**E06-Q02**).
- Functional testing of production engine features (none exist yet; that is E11's QA).
- Backend load testing (k6/Locust), which belongs to E03/E07/E08.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A second engineer reproduces the numbers from the README alone
  Given a clean checkout and the package README
  When an engineer who did not write the harness runs B1, B3, B4 and B5 on a second reference-class machine
  Then they obtain results without asking the author any questions
  And the per-scenario delta between the two machines is recorded as the documented noise band

Scenario: The noise band is small enough to decide a 10 % criterion
  Given the documented cross-machine and run-to-run noise band
  When it is compared to ADR-0011 criterion 1's 10 % threshold
  Then the noise band is materially smaller than 10 %, or the harness is changed (more repetitions, longer runs, tighter environment control) until it is
  And the achieved noise band is stated in the M0 report so readers can judge every comparison themselves

Scenario: Guards actually guard
  Given deliberately malformed runs
  When a 2-repetition run, a run with a missing GPU descriptor and a run with a mismatched fixture hash are each attempted
  Then the first is marked "not admissible for ADR evidence", and the second and third fail outright
  And none of the three silently produces a normal-looking report

Scenario: Instrumentation does not change the result it reports
  Given the same scenario run with and without stage instrumentation
  When p95 frame times are compared
  Then the difference is <= 3 %, or the overhead is documented and consistently subtracted with the method stated

Scenario: QA gates the evidence, not the opinion
  Given methodology defects of severity major or above are open
  When E06-T02 attempts to publish the report as ADR evidence
  Then publication is blocked until the defects are resolved or explicitly accepted with the Architect's recorded rationale
```

## Technical notes / design
- The reproducer must use a machine matching the reference class in `06-…` §3.1 (6c/12t x86_64, 32 GB, NVMe, GTX 1650 / Iris Xe class GPU). Record both machines' full descriptors; a cross-class comparison would measure hardware, not noise.
- Run-to-run noise and machine-to-machine noise are different quantities and must be reported separately — the former governs whether a re-run changed anything, the latter governs whether two engineers' numbers can be compared at all.
- Thermal effects: note whether runs were done on a warm or cold machine, and prescribe A/B/A alternation for any comparison (as E06-T01 does across runtimes).
- Defects found here are filed against **E06-K01** with severity, not fixed inside this ticket — QA validates, engineering fixes, so the audit trail stays honest.

## Test plan
- **Review**: line-by-line check of the harness against `06-…` §7.1-§7.4, producing a checklist with pass/fail per requirement.
- **Reproduction**: 4 scenarios x 3 repetitions on the second machine; deltas tabulated.
- **Negative**: the three guard tests above, automated so they remain true after the spike (they live in the harness's own unit suite).
- **Exploratory** (per `03-testing-strategy.md` §11): a timeboxed 2 h charter on the harness itself — what happens on a machine with no discrete GPU, with the page backgrounded mid-run, with the window resized mid-run, with the system under heavy CPU load? Each finding recorded as "expected / defect / needs decision".
- **Documentation**: README walkthrough defects filed.
- Coverage: the negative-guard tests count toward the harness package's >= 85 % threshold.

## Security notes
- Verify the harness performs **no network I/O** during a run (STRIDE **T**ampering — a fixture silently sourced from the internet would invalidate determinism and introduce a supply-chain path). Assert by monitoring during a run, not only by code reading.
- Confirm report artefacts contain no machine-identifying data beyond hardware class and no absolute paths with usernames (STRIDE **I**nformation disclosure, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5).
- Data classification: none.

## Accessibility notes
QA verifies that the **DOM-mirror sync** stage appears in the harness's stage list and is non-zero when the mirror stub is active (**E06-D03**) — an a11y cost silently reported as zero would understate the engine's real budget consumption, which is exactly the failure mode `06-…` §4.3 guards against by giving it a named 1 ms slice.

## Performance notes
This ticket sets the credibility of every performance number in the Epic: the documented noise band, the instrumentation overhead figure, and the repetition policy. Those three numbers appear in the M0 report's methodology section.

## Observability
Produces the methodology section of the M0 report and the permanent negative-guard tests that keep the harness honest for the life of the engine package.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Methodology checklist completed with pass/fail per `06-…` §7.1-§7.4 requirement.
- [ ] Independent reproduction completed on a second reference-class machine; noise bands (run-to-run and machine-to-machine) documented.
- [ ] Noise band confirmed materially below ADR-0011's 10 % threshold, or harness changes made until it is.
- [ ] Negative-guard tests merged and green.
- [ ] Exploratory charter executed and findings triaged.
- [ ] README defects filed against E06-K01 and resolved or accepted.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted; E06-T02 unblocked.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E06-K01` — the harness is the object under validation.
- Blocks **E06-T02** — results may not be published as ADR evidence without this sign-off.

## Branch
`test/e06-bench-methodology` (negative-guard tests + methodology doc). PR size guidance: one PR, tests + docs.

## References
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §2 (architecture), §3.4 (GL backend), §3.6 (LOD), §3.7 (SDF text), §3.8 (heatmap streaming), §13 (benchmarks B1-B10), §14 (test strategy), §15 (milestone M0), §16 (open items O1-O3)

title: GPU/browser compatibility sweep and degraded-2d exploratory charter
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` carries **R8 Browser/GPU compat** as a standing risk, and the engine design answers it with a capability probe that selects one of three render profiles — `full`, `reduced`, `degraded-2d` (`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.4) — plus an explicit claim in §2 that when `OffscreenCanvas` is unavailable "the same worker code runs on the main thread behind an identical facade (`RunMode.inline`); only throughput changes, not behaviour. This is a supported, tested mode, not an accident."

Two claims there are untested: that `degraded-2d` is a *supported profile* rather than a euphemism for a broken chart, and that `RunMode.inline` changes throughput but not behaviour. Both matter beyond the spike — managers may use the browser rather than the desktop shell (`ADR-0011`: "The browser remains a fully supported deployment target for managers"), so the browser path is a real product surface, not a fallback nobody uses.

The compatibility findings also feed E06-T01: the matrix needs to know what "reference hardware" deliberately excludes, so the report does not over-claim from a single favourable GPU.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Capability/compatibility sweep** of the prototype (scenes A and B, plus C where capabilities allow) across:
  - Chrome/Chromium, Edge and Firefox on the reference machine (the browser deployment target);
  - a low-end integrated-GPU machine (Intel UHD class — below the reference bar, deliberately) to force `reduced` and `degraded-2d` profiles;
  - a machine with a deliberately outdated GPU driver, to see what an un-updated user actually experiences;
  - software rendering (SwiftShader / `--disable-gpu`) as the floor case.
- **Capability probe result table** per environment: max texture size, max texture units, `EXT_color_buffer_float`, `OES_texture_float_linear`, `R16F` render/sample, instancing, integer attributes, max vertex attributes, `OffscreenCanvas` in a worker — the same list ADR-0011 criterion 4 requires, extended to browsers.
- **`degraded-2d` evaluation**: with the GL path forced off, is the chart usable? Does the Canvas-2D path render correct (if coarser) output, is footprint limited to L2/L3 as designed (§3.7), and what is the honest frame rate? Recorded as a usability verdict, not only a number.
- **`RunMode.inline` behavioural-equivalence check**: the same scenario run in worker mode and inline mode, with outputs compared for behavioural identity (same LOD decisions, same rendered geometry, same interaction semantics) and throughput reported separately.
- **Exploratory charters** (per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11), timeboxed 2 h each, findings triaged as expected/defect/needs-decision:
  1. *Context loss and recovery*: force `WEBGL_lose_context` at varied moments (mid-pan, mid-upload, during atlas generation) and observe recovery against the documented behaviour (`26-…` §3.4).
  2. *Hostile display conditions*: fractional DPR (1.25, 1.5, 1.75), browser zoom to 200 % (required by `26-…` §12 reflow rule), monitor switch mid-session, HDR display, multi-monitor with mixed DPI.
  3. *Resource starvation*: heavy CPU load, another GPU-hungry tab, backgrounded tab (rAF throttling), laptop on battery saver.
- **Chaos scenario** contribution back to `03-testing-strategy.md` §9's catalogue: the context-loss scenario as a reusable, documented test for E11.

## Out of scope
- Mobile browsers and Android (out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14).
- Safari/macOS unless a machine is available — record as a gap with an owner rather than silently omitting it, since WKWebView is the Tauri path on macOS.
- Fixing what is found: defects are filed against the scene tickets or recorded as E11 constraints.
- Performance verdicts on the reference machine (**E06-T01**) — this ticket is about the edges, not the centre.

### Scope trim (21-point roadmap budget)
The sweep covers **three GPU/driver classes** — NVIDIA discrete (GTX 1650 class), Intel Iris Xe integrated, and one software/ANGLE fallback path — the minimum needed to characterise risk **R8**. A wider device matrix is deferred to **E46 Performance hardening**; this ticket records the classes *not* covered as a known gap in the M0 report.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every environment yields a profile decision, not a crash
  Given each environment in the sweep
  When the capability probe runs and the prototype loads
  Then a render profile (full / reduced / degraded-2d) is selected and the scene renders correct output at that profile
  And any environment where the prototype fails to render at all is recorded as a defect with the probe output attached

Scenario: degraded-2d is usable, and we say how usable
  Given the GL path is forced off
  When scenes A and B render through the Canvas-2D path
  Then footprint is limited to L2/L3 per 26-chart-engine-design.md §3.7 and candles/axes still render correctly
  And an honest frame-rate figure and usability verdict are recorded, rather than the mode being described only as "supported"

Scenario: Inline mode changes throughput, not behaviour
  Given the same scenario in worker mode and in RunMode.inline
  When outputs are compared
  Then LOD decisions, rendered geometry and interaction semantics are identical
  And any behavioural difference is filed as a defect against the claim in 26-chart-engine-design.md §2

Scenario: Context loss recovers as documented
  Given WEBGL_lose_context is triggered mid-pan, mid-upload and during atlas generation
  When the context is restored
  Then the engine stops the loop, invalidates GPU resources, rebuilds from the data model and resumes with at most a one-frame flash and no data loss
  And any case that loses data or fails to recover is a defect, not an accepted limitation

Scenario: Browser zoom to 200 % reflows rather than clips
  Given browser zoom is increased to 200 %
  When the chart renders
  Then density classes scale and content is not clipped, per 26-chart-engine-design.md §12
  And the resulting cell sizes are checked against E06-D01's legibility thresholds
```

## Technical notes / design
- The probe table is the durable artefact: E11 will use it to decide which capabilities may be assumed and which need a fallback path. Capture raw probe output, not a summary.
- Fractional DPR is a known source of hairline and text-crispness bugs given the engine's pixel-snapping strategy (§3.4); examine rendered output visually, not only frame times.
- Backgrounded-tab rAF throttling interacts with the render-on-demand design (§3.2 rule 5) and with the heatmap's 10 Hz cadence: when the tab returns to the foreground, does the heatmap catch up correctly or replay a burst? A burst on return is a real production concern for a trader switching windows.
- Outdated-driver environments are where `EXT_color_buffer_float` tends to go missing, which forces the heatmap to a lower-precision format — record what visual difference that actually makes.
- Software rendering will be far below budget; the question is whether the app degrades gracefully and says so (the SCR-030 "low-GPU degraded" state and the SCR-048 WebGL-unavailable messaging), not whether it is fast.

## Test plan
- Sweep executed per environment with the capability probe and scenes A/B (C where supported), results tabulated.
- Three exploratory charters executed, timeboxed, with session notes recorded per `03-testing-strategy.md` §11.
- Worker-vs-inline behavioural comparison via golden images plus a LOD-decision trace diff.
- Context-loss chaos scenario documented for reuse and contributed to the §9 catalogue.
- Findings triaged with the chart-engine lead; each becomes a defect, an E11 constraint, or an accepted limitation with rationale.

## Security notes
- Testing across machines must not introduce unpinned tooling: each environment uses the same pinned harness build (STRIDE **T**ampering, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §12).
- No credentials or real data on any test machine; synthetic fixtures only. Data classification: none.
- The outdated-driver machine is deliberately unpatched for testing and must not be used for anything else; record it as an isolated test asset so it never becomes a shadow workstation.

## Accessibility notes
- Browser zoom to 200 % is a WCAG 2.2 reflow requirement (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, `26-…` §12) and is tested here as a first-class scenario.
- `degraded-2d` must not lose the accessible layer: the DOM mirror and data cursor are DOM-based and independent of the GL path, so the sweep verifies a11y behaviour is unchanged across all three render profiles (also an acceptance criterion of **E06-D03**).
- The "reduced live detail" indicator required by `06-…` §4.4 must be non-colour-only; check its presence wherever degradation engages.

## Performance notes
Not a budget-verification ticket. It produces the *context* for the budget numbers: which environments meet the reference bar, which degrade, and what degradation actually delivers. Feeds the M0 report's compatibility section.

## Observability
Capability probe output is captured into the harness report per environment, so any future benchmark result carries the capability context that produced it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Sweep completed across all listed environments (or gaps recorded with owners, e.g. macOS/WKWebView).
- [ ] Capability probe table published and handed to E11.
- [ ] `degraded-2d` usability verdict and frame-rate figures recorded.
- [ ] Worker-vs-inline behavioural-equivalence result recorded; defects filed if they differ.
- [ ] Three exploratory charters executed with session notes; findings triaged.
- [ ] Context-loss chaos scenario documented and contributed to `03-testing-strategy.md` §9.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted; findings handed to **E06-T01** and **E06-T02**.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E06-K02, E06-K03` — needs renderable scenes; scene C is included where the environment supports it.
- Blocks **E06-T01** (the matrix needs to know what reference hardware excludes).

`test/e06-compat-sweep` (probe tables, charters, chaos scenario docs). PR size guidance: docs + test-scenario definitions, one PR.

title: STRIDE model of the engine and desktop-shell boundary; hardening checklist
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 requires a STRIDE kickoff for any Epic touching a trust boundary, and `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 names STRIDE models for E03, E08 and E09 as R0 quality gates. E06 is not on that list because the spike itself handles no secrets — but it **chooses the desktop shell**, and the shell is one of the product's most consequential trust boundaries (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §4). Choosing it on performance numbers alone, then discovering afterwards what hardening costs, would be exactly backwards.

`ADR-0011` makes this concrete in two places. Its "Interim consequences" list Electron's security posture as requiring deliberate hardening — `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `sandbox: true`, strict CSP, an allow-list preload, navigation and `window.open` blocked, signed auto-updates — and notes these are "mandatory checklist items in `04-security-program.md`, not defaults". And its **criterion 5** requires, for Tauri to be adoptable, "a documented, working equivalent of every shell responsibility: OS-keychain bridge for the KEK, auto-update with signature verification, deep links, multi-window workspace persistence, and Playwright-drivable E2E". Criterion 5 is a security deliverable wearing an architecture hat, and without a checklist it is unfalsifiable prose.

This ticket therefore does two things: models the threats, and turns criterion 5 into a checkable list that **E06-T01** applies and **E06-T03** decides against.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **STRIDE threat model** for this Epic's scope, following `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5's method and recorded in the security programme's model set:
  - *Assets*: the desktop shell's privilege boundary, the KEK held in the OS keychain (`ADR-0009`), the auto-update channel, the rendering pipeline's inputs (WS frames, shaders, fonts), the diagnostics payload.
  - *Trust boundaries*: renderer <-> preload <-> main process (Electron) or WebView <-> Rust host (Tauri); web page <-> shared worker; app <-> OS keychain; app <-> update server.
  - *Threats per STRIDE category*, at minimum: **S** — a malicious page impersonating the app's deep-link handler; **T** — supply-chain tampering of engine/bench dependencies, font or shader assets, unsigned updates; **R** — none material at this layer, stated explicitly; **I** — diagnostics payload leaking account/user context (SCR-046 "copy diagnostics"), the DOM-mirror reproducing sensitive values into the DOM, GPU memory residue; **D** — context-loss loops, unbounded ring growth, a rogue WS producing upload storms; **E** — `nodeIntegration` or a permissive preload granting a compromised renderer OS access, WebView2's OS-updated component changing behaviour under the app.
  - Each threat: likelihood, impact, existing control, required control, owner, and whether it is an E06 action or an E10/E11 constraint.
- **Shell hardening checklist** (the measurable form of ADR-0011 criterion 5), covering both candidates, each item stated as a verifiable check:
  - `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `sandbox: true`, strict CSP with no `unsafe-eval`, allow-list preload exposing a named API surface only, navigation and `window.open` blocked by default, remote module disabled;
  - OS-keychain bridge able to store and retrieve the KEK per `ADR-0009`, with the failure mode when the keychain is unavailable;
  - auto-update with signature verification and a documented rollback;
  - deep-link handling that validates and refuses unexpected schemes/targets;
  - multi-window workspace persistence without writing secrets to disk in plaintext;
  - Playwright-drivable E2E (a shell that cannot be automated cannot be regression-tested, which is itself a security property).
- **Applied to the harness shells**: E06-T01's Electron and Tauri harnesses must be built with these settings on, so the measured numbers are numbers we can actually ship against.
- **Abuse cases** for the diagnostics payload (E06-D02) and for the engine's input surface, written as concrete misuse scenarios with expected defences.
- Handoff of the checklist and the unresolved constraints to **E10** (shell implementation) and **E11** (engine).

## Out of scope
- Implementing the hardening in the production shell — **E10**.
- Auth, RBAC, session handling, API-key storage — **E09** and the ACCT domain.
- Backend threat models (exchange boundary E08, supply chain E03, auth E09) — separately gated in `30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4.
- Penetration testing, which `04-security-program.md` §13 schedules before Live enablement (R4).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The model covers every STRIDE category explicitly
  Given the threat model for E06's scope
  When it is reviewed against docs/plan/04-security-program.md §5
  Then each of the six STRIDE categories has either at least one identified threat with a control, or an explicit "not material here, because…" statement
  And no category is silently omitted

Scenario: Criterion 5 becomes checkable
  Given ADR-0011 criterion 5's five shell responsibilities
  When the hardening checklist is published
  Then each responsibility maps to one or more items that a reviewer can mark pass or fail by observation
  And E06-T01 can execute the checklist against both candidate shells without further interpretation

Scenario: Harness shells are hardened before they are measured
  Given the Electron and Tauri harness shells used by E06-T01
  When their configuration is inspected
  Then contextIsolation is true, nodeIntegration is false, sandbox is true and a strict CSP is in force
  And any hardening item that could not be enabled in the harness is recorded with its expected performance implication, so the measurement's validity is known

Scenario: The diagnostics payload cannot leak context
  Given the SCR-046 "copy diagnostics" payload specified in E06-D02
  When it is reviewed against the abuse cases
  Then the allowed field list contains no user identifier, no account context, no symbol-linked order correlation id
  And a violation of that list is defined as a security defect, not a product decision

Scenario: Unresolved risks land on an owning epic
  Given threats that E06 cannot close inside its scope
  When the model is finalised
  Then each is recorded as a named constraint on E10 or E11 with an owner
  And none is left owned by the closed spike
```

## Technical notes / design
- Electron's hardening settings have measurable cost (sandboxing and context isolation add IPC overhead), which is exactly why they must be on during measurement rather than bolted on after the shell is chosen — a hardened-vs-unhardened delta should also be recorded, since it is useful evidence in its own right.
- WebView2's OS-updated nature is a security property as well as a performance one: the app cannot pin the engine it runs on, so the model must state what changes when Microsoft ships a new WebView2 (both the benefit — security patches arrive without us shipping — and the risk — behaviour changes under the application).
- Electron's counterpart is the Chromium update treadmill: we own shipping security patches. Name the owner and the cadence as a required control if Electron wins.
- Shader and font assets must be vendored and pinned, not fetched — the SDF atlas is generated at runtime from the design-system font (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.7), which makes the font an executable-adjacent input.
- The DOM mirror reproduces rendered values into the DOM; in production that inherits the chart's data classification. Record it now so E11 does not treat the mirror as an unclassified invisible surface.

## Test plan
- Threat model reviewed in a working session with the Architect and the chart-engine lead (per `04-security-program.md` §5's process), findings minuted.
- Checklist dry-run against the harness shells before E06-T01's matrix begins; each item marked pass/fail with evidence.
- Abuse cases exercised against the diagnostics payload spec: attempt to include a user id, an account id and an order correlation id, and confirm the spec's field allow-list rejects each.
- Negative check on the harness: confirm no network egress during a run (shared with E06-Q01), since the shell's network posture is part of the boundary.
- Security-tooling gates per `04-security-program.md` §12 apply to any merged code (harness): Semgrep/CodeQL, npm audit, gitleaks.

## Security notes
This ticket **is** the Epic's security deliverable. Data classification for the spike itself: none (synthetic data, no credentials, no PII). The classification that matters is the one the chosen shell will later hold — the KEK — which is why criterion 5's keychain item is non-negotiable and is reviewed by the Security engineer before **E06-T03** finalises the ADR.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no user surface. One intersection worth recording: `role="application"` on the chart wrapper (`26-…` §12) hands keystrokes to the app, so the shell's global shortcut registry (E10) and the engine's keyboard handling must not create a state where a user cannot escape the canvas. Recorded here as a constraint for E10 rather than a threat.

## Performance notes
Hardening settings are enabled during measurement, and the hardened-vs-unhardened delta is recorded, so the M0 report's numbers reflect a shippable configuration rather than a permissive one.

## Observability
Required controls include: audit-relevant shell events (update applied, update signature failure, deep link refused) defined now so E10 implements them, and the diagnostics-payload field allow-list, which becomes a reviewable constant rather than ad hoc serialisation.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] STRIDE model complete, all six categories addressed, reviewed and minuted with Architect + chart-engine lead.
- [ ] Shell hardening checklist published and handed to **E06-T01** before the matrix runs.
- [ ] Harness shells verified hardened; any exception recorded with its performance implication.
- [ ] Abuse cases for the diagnostics payload executed against E06-D02's spec; field allow-list agreed.
- [ ] Unresolved threats recorded as named constraints on E10/E11 with owners.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment posted.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated where the model surfaced or retired a risk.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E01` — needs the governance baseline (`SECURITY.md`, CODEOWNERS, the security review process) that defines how a model is recorded and signed off.
- Blocks **E06-T01** (hardened harness shells) and feeds **E06-T03** (criterion 5 evaluation).

title: Pin and scan spike toolchain; enforce throwaway-code containment
body:
## Context
A spike is where supply-chain discipline usually slips: throwaway code invites throwaway dependency hygiene, and the Tauri arm adds an entire second toolchain (Rust, crates, WebView2) to a repo that otherwise has none. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §12 mandates SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep), SCA (Dependabot/npm audit/pip-audit), secrets scanning (gitleaks) and container scanning as CI gates — with no exemption for exploratory work, because a compromised dev dependency runs on developer machines and in CI with exactly the privileges the pipeline has.

There is a second, subtler containment problem. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.2 requires that spike code be "either promoted (with normal Task/Story DoD then applying to the promoted portion) or explicitly marked throwaway and the branch left unmerged/archived". E06 has a deliberate split — the **harness and fixture generator are promoted** (merged, tested, covered), while the **three prototype scenes are throwaway** (never merged). Without an enforced boundary, prototype-quality code with no tests and no coverage leaks into `packages/chart-engine` and becomes the foundation E11 unknowingly builds on. That is the most expensive possible outcome of a cheap spike.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Dependency pinning and review** for everything the spike introduces:
  - JS/TS: Playwright, Electron, benchmark tooling, any GL helper libraries — exact versions, lockfile committed, no ranges; each new direct dependency justified in the PR description (what it does, why not hand-rolled, maintenance status).
  - Rust/Tauri arm: crate set pinned via `Cargo.lock`, `cargo audit` run, and the arm's dependencies explicitly marked as **spike-only** so they do not silently become production dependencies if Tauri is rejected.
  - Vendored assets: the design-system font used for SDF generation (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.7) pinned and checksummed in-repo, never fetched at build or run time.
- **CI gates applied to the spike surface**: npm audit / Dependabot coverage for the new packages, gitleaks on the spike branch, Semgrep/CodeQL on the merged harness code, `cargo audit` for the Tauri arm — per `04-security-program.md` §12.
- **Throwaway-code containment**, enforced not merely documented:
  - prototype scenes live under a clearly named directory (e.g. `packages/chart-engine/spike/`) on the spike branch only;
  - a CI check on `main` that fails if that path exists, so prototype code cannot arrive by accident;
  - `import-linter`-style or ESLint boundary rule ensuring the merged harness never imports from the spike path;
  - README banners in the prototype stating throwaway status, date, and the report that supersedes it.
- **Branch archival procedure**: on Epic close, `spike/e06-engine-m0` is tagged and archived unmerged, with the tag recorded on the Epic and in the M0 report so the prototype remains findable without being importable.
- **Secrets hygiene check**: confirm no `.env`, no tokens, no machine-identifying paths in committed benchmark artefacts (shared concern with E06-Q01 and E06-T02).

## Out of scope
- Production dependency policy for the engine package — E11 inherits the policy but sets its own dependency set.
- Container scanning (Trivy) and image hardening — E03's pipeline scope; this ticket only ensures the spike's additions are inside the existing gates.
- Rust toolchain policy for the wider project: if Tauri is rejected in **E06-T03**, the Rust arm's dependencies are removed entirely, which is the cleanest possible outcome and should be executed rather than left dormant.
- The threat model itself (**E06-X01**).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Nothing the spike adds is unpinned
  Given every dependency introduced by E06 across JS and Rust
  When the lockfiles and manifests are reviewed
  Then each is pinned to an exact version with a lockfile entry
  And each new direct dependency has a written justification in its introducing PR

Scenario: Scanners actually cover the new surface
  Given the merged harness and the spike branch
  When CI runs
  Then npm audit / Dependabot, gitleaks and Semgrep/CodeQL report on the new paths
  And cargo audit runs for the Tauri arm, with findings triaged rather than ignored as "just a spike"

Scenario: Prototype code cannot reach main
  Given a PR that includes files under the spike directory
  When CI runs on that PR targeting main
  Then the containment check fails with a message explaining the promoted-vs-throwaway split
  And the check is verified by a deliberate test PR before the Epic closes

Scenario: The harness does not depend on the prototype
  Given the merged benchmark harness
  When its imports are analysed
  Then it imports nothing from the spike path
  And the boundary is enforced by a lint rule, not by reviewer vigilance

Scenario: Artefacts carry no secrets or identifying data
  Given committed benchmark report artefacts
  When they are scanned
  Then no tokens, credentials, internal hostnames or absolute paths containing usernames are present
  And gitleaks passes on the spike branch as well as on main

Scenario: The branch is archived, not abandoned
  Given the Epic reaches Done
  When the spike branch is disposed of
  Then it is tagged and archived unmerged, with the tag recorded on the Epic and in the M0 report
  And no prototype commit has been merged into main
```

## Technical notes / design
- The containment CI check is deliberately crude and therefore reliable: a path-existence assertion on `main` plus an import-boundary lint rule. Sophisticated policy engines fail silently; a path check does not.
- Rust-arm dependencies should be confined to a workspace member that is trivially deletable, so rejecting Tauri is a directory removal rather than an archaeology exercise.
- Font vendoring: record the font's SHA-256 alongside the asset, and have the atlas generator assert the hash at generation time — a swapped font silently changes every glyph metric and therefore every text benchmark.
- Dependabot noise on spike-only dependencies is acceptable while the spike is live and should be shut off by deleting the dependencies afterwards, not by muting the scanner.
- Coordinate with **E03**: the gates exist in the pipeline; this ticket ensures E06's paths are inside their scope rather than accidentally excluded by path filters.

## Test plan
- **Negative CI test**: a deliberate PR adding a file under the spike path to `main` must fail the containment check; recorded as evidence.
- **Negative lint test**: a deliberate import from the harness into the spike path must fail the boundary rule.
- **Scanner verification**: confirm each gate reports on the new paths (not merely that the job ran) by checking the scanned-file lists.
- **Hash test**: altering the vendored font causes the atlas generator's hash assertion to fail.
- Coverage: containment and boundary checks are CI configuration plus one small script; the script carries the package coverage threshold.

## Security notes
This ticket is the supply-chain control for the Epic, mapping to STRIDE **T**ampering in **E06-X01**'s model: pinned dependencies, scanned surfaces, vendored assets with hash assertions, no run-time fetching, and secrets scanning on both the spike branch and `main`. It also addresses a modest **I**nformation-disclosure risk in committed artefacts (machine-identifying paths). Data classification: none — but the controls are the same ones production depends on, which is precisely why the spike may not be exempt.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — CI and dependency controls, no user surface.

## Performance notes
One indirect effect worth stating: pinning tooling versions is a prerequisite for comparable benchmark results over time. An unpinned Playwright, Electron or Chromium turns a benchmark baseline into a moving target, so this ticket also protects `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §7.4's baseline policy.

## Observability
CI surfaces scanner findings per path; the containment check's failure message is written to be self-explanatory so a future contributor understands the promoted-vs-throwaway split without reading this ticket.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All spike-introduced dependencies pinned with committed lockfiles and written justifications.
- [ ] npm audit/Dependabot, gitleaks, Semgrep/CodeQL and cargo audit confirmed covering the new paths; findings triaged.
- [ ] Containment CI check and import-boundary lint rule merged and verified by deliberate failing test PRs.
- [ ] Vendored font pinned with a hash assertion in the atlas generator.
- [ ] Benchmark artefacts confirmed free of secrets and identifying paths.
- [ ] Spike branch archival procedure documented; executed at Epic close with the tag recorded.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment posted.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E06-K01` — the harness is the thing being pinned and scanned.
- `blocked_by: E06-X01` — containment and pinning are controls the threat model specifies; doing them first would be guessing at the requirement.
- Relies on **E03**'s pipeline for the underlying scanner jobs.

`chore/e06-spike-supply-chain`. PR size guidance: small, <= 200 LOC of CI/lint configuration plus docs; the deliberate failing test PRs are closed, not merged.
